Two employees were taken to the emergency room at Denver General for oxygen and observation after being exposed to carbon monoxide from a propane heater being used indoors.
Employee was hospitalized as a result of a fall from approximately 19 feet when a scaffold brace failed and the scaffold collapsed.
A maintenance employee who was clearing snow fell while walking across the driveway.  The employee struck his/her head, requiring an in-patient hospitalization.
Employee partially amputated the left tip of his pinky and 1/3 of his ring finger on the left hand while setting up a Flexographic Printer.

An employee was hospitalized from injuries he received when he fell off of a ladder.  The employee put an aluminum ladder in the bed of his truck and leaned it against a power line to cut a telephone line.  The employee fell on the concrete area below.

An employee had just finished unloading a shipment of cardboard boxes.  The cardboard boxes were on pallets; the individual pallets and stacks of cardboard boxes were secured with banding straps.  The employee grabbed and pulled on a banding strap on one of the pallets to try and straighten the pallet by a few inches to align with the other pallets.  When the employee pulled on the banding strap, the strap broke and the employee fell to the floor.  The employee broke his left hip.  The employee was hospitalized for hip surgery.
A metal plate fell off of a forklift and hit an employee standing in the area, injuring the employee's foot.

Employees were installing a pump at the facility. During the process, the pump shifted and caught one of the employees fingers, smashing it against the pedestal wall of the pump. Employee was transported to the Memorial Herman Hospital where they determined that the finger had a fracture.
Employee was exiting work vehicle and caught finger in driver-side door, resulting in the amputation of the employee's right middle fingertip.
A maintenance employee slipped on ice while applying salt to ice on the ground in the fenced-in yard of the facility.  He slipped and broke his left fibula and dislocated his left ankle.
The employee was working in the bakery pulling a stock cart when the cart caught her in the heel and knocked her shoe off.  The employee tripped over the shoe, causing her to fall on her left hip.

Employee was loading boxes onto a conveyor belt when his glove got caught in the belt. As a result, the employee lost the tip of his left index finger. The worker was taken to a nearby clinic and was then transported to a Reconstructive Orthopedic Center located at 1200 Binz St. Houston, TX 77004.
Employee was loading the cargo hold and started to close the cargo door.  The door snapped back and caught his finger, amputating his right index finger at the first digit.
An employee fell 12 feet to the ground from the top of the top wagon, resulting in a broken left elbow. He was admitted to the hospital for surgery.
Employees were making a connection when tubing fell striking the employee in the lower face.
Employee inhaled paint fumes and was taken to the hospital.

Employee was leaving a private residence where she had provided home health care and slipped on a snow-covered handicap ramp.  Employee was transported to the Hospital of Central Connecticut New Britain Campus where she was admitted and treated for a fractured left ankle.
An employee working off site at a health fair slipped and fell on the ice in the parking lot.  The employee broke the right fibula, leading to an in-patient hospitalization and surgical treatment.
An employee's left thumb was cut deeply while operating a meat band saw.

At approximately 3:45 PM on 3/4/15, an employee was operating a pneumatic assembly fixture with two handed controls. The fixture's drive cylinder pinched off the tip of his left ring finger. The cylinder pulled off half the employee's fingernail and tissue, leaving the bone.
On 2/4/15, an employee was standing on a pallet moving stock and tripped, resulting in a broken hip.
An employee was inspecting an out-of-service water pipe.  The pipe had accumulated high alkaline water.  The employee received chemical burns to the feet, ankles, and calves.

On February 4, 2015, at approximately 11:15 a.m., an employee working on an upper level of a new medical center construction at 505 Baxter Parkway in Social Circle, Georgia, descended a caged ladder to get something to eat.  The employee fell an estimated 10 or 12 feet to a lower level, suffering a fractured L-1 vertebrae, and was airlifted to the Gwinnett Medical Center in Lawrenceville, Georgia, where he was admitted and scheduled for surgery.
Employee was carrying tar paper on the roof when he slipped on the roof's wet surface and fell from a two-story house, fracturing his lower back.
An employee was cutting a branch from a tree using a chain saw. The branch fell striking the employee in the chest and knocking him to the ground injuring his back and chest.

Worker was walking out from the building and was struck on the head by a falling piece of metal that was removed from an upper level window. Worker was taken to Methodist Hospital at 6565 Fanning St. in Houston, Texas, where personnel stitched his head.

Employee was sitting at the kitchen table of a customer's house filling out paperwork when the chair broke underneath him.  The employee fell and hit his neck, suffering a herniated disk in his neck that will require surgery.
An employee missed the step while exiting the ambulance and fell from the ambulance rear door, striking his head.

Employee was injured in a motor vehicle accident while traveling from his office to another location for a meeting.  Employee suffered head injuries in the accident and was transported to the emergency room and admitted for continued treatment.

Employee was cutting chicken at his work station on the deboning line. The chicken slipped to the floor, and the employee reached to pick it up with knife still in hand. The employee punctured his eye with the knife while picking the chicken up toward himself and required hospitalization.

On 2/4/15, worker was operating a Trumf press brake when the punch came down on his fingers while he was setting the press up to operate.  Specifically, the worker was placing a polyurethane cover over the die so that the part to be processed would not be damaged. The worker stepped forward on the foot pedal, which activated the press and injured multiple fingers.  The worker was hospitalized following surgery to place pins in the injured fingers.

The employee was unloading a flatbed semi trailer. The forklift operator was removing material from the trailer. The material began shifting on the forks, and the employee moved to avoid being struck. The employee lost his footing and fell off of the trailer, fracturing his pelvis.

Employee was offloading a structural beam in a laydown yard.  When the beam was lowered, it rotated, and the employee's hand was caught between the cribbing and bracing.  As a result, the employee broke his third, fourth, and fifth fingers (metacarpals). The employee was hospitalized later that day.

An employee fell approximately 12 feet from the top of a DOT water tank at the Naval Shipyard on February 2, 2015. The employee had been filling the tank with waste water from a naval vessel. They had just completed the job when it started to rain. The supervisor or team leader asked the victim to climb up and close the top hatch.  The victim fell off, landed head first on the asphalt, and required hospitalization.
Employee lost a fingertip when an internal pipe valve was activated. The employee bumped the emergency shut off with his body and the valve shut on his finger.
The employee was using a miter saw to cut pieces of aluminum that were to be assembled into prototypes for the organization. His thumb was jerked into the saw and was cut.
An employee unstrapping unit #6 on top of his truck slipped on ice and fell approximately 8 feet, fracturing his elbow.
Employee cut off tip of left thumb while preparing arts and crafts materials using a paper cutter.

An employee was taking the bolts out of an 8-inch flange when the 40 lb. flange fell 1 inch onto his left pointer finger, resulting in a laceration. The finger had to be amputated at the knuckle at York Hospital.

Employee was operating a roll mill swedger. He was pushing on a slide bar when he placed his right hand on the moving equipment, severely crushing his middle finger.  He was taken to the hospital where the tip of his right middle finger was amputated at the first joint.
An employee was injured by a utility knife. He was cutting banding on a wood bundle when the knife slipped, and he cut his left forearm.
An employee was kept overnight at the hospital for treatment of exposure to 10% nitric oxide that began to leak from a #49 cylinder at the roller table.
An employee was installing an underground piping fitting connection with mechanical equipment and received a severe injury when caught between the mechanical fitting equipment and the trench shoring.

On February 5, 2015 an employee working at the Genesis Community Center tripped over a curb in the parking lot suffering a dislocated shoulder.  The employee was hospitalized due to the severity of the injury.
An employee severed a finger while working at the lathe machine.

An employee was tightening a bolt on a 16" pipe flange located 6" off the floor with a 3/4" ratchet wrench.  The wrench broke, causing the employee to fall backwards and hit the ground.  Upon falling to the ground, the employee's leg was fractured.
Employee's finger was amputated when caught in spot welder.
An employee #1 operating a picker was struck by the load of a second picker, resulting in multiple leg fractures to employee #1.
Employee fell from ladder while painting.
Employer reports hospitalization due to an employee tripping on an area rug that was not secured to the floor at Disney Hollywood Studios-Tower of Terror.
A federal prison inmate was cleaning the floor with compressed air when the inmate tripped on a metal frame and fell resulting in a broken right forearm. The inmate was admitted to the hospital.

An employee at a remote Marathon Oil jobsite was pressure testing pipe when he was struck-by 9500psi of water when bolts broke on the flange connecting two pipes causing the high pressure water to strike the employee and one other sub-contractor's employee who were standing approximately 15 feet away.
An employee fell from a beam he was standing on, down to a catwalk below, when he was removing rust from another beam. The employee sustained neck and back injuries.

Employee was taking papers out to a truck driver. She left the office through the south office door. Walking to the truck, she slipped on ice in the parking lot and fell. She landed on her left hip, striking the ground. She injured her left hip and possibly her back. She was transported to Mercy Hospital in Springfield, Missouri, where she was admitted.
An employee suffered an amputation of the tip of his right ring finger while adjusting the platen on the 7202 printing press.

An employee passed out and was found unconscious. The employee regained consciousness and was found to have a gash near the right temple. Blood was observed on a parts cart and the floor where the employee was first found. EMS responded and took the employee to Doctor's West Hospital. A cat scan was performed and the employee was found to have minor internal brain bleeding. The employee was taken to Grant Hospital for further tests.

Incident occurred right outside the test bay in the Conroe Facility.  Employees were working on a pump unit skid simultaneously. The lead man and assembly technician were working on the control panel. The injured employee was laying on the left side between the radiator housing assembly and the fan belt assembly. Injured employee reached up to grab and hold the wrench (to "hold backstop") at the same time that the assembly technician hooked up the airline from the start exhaust to the throttle exhaust. As soon as the engine started (by plugging in the airline), the injured employee jerked his left arm back. The motion caused the injured employee's right arm to move up. The sleeve of his shirt was caught by the fan belt. When he went to pull away from the fan belt, his hand got caught in the fan belt. The fan belt ran his hand through the pulley, causing partial amputation of his right ring finger, an abrasion to his middle finger, and bruising/abrasion to his right arm.
An employee fractured his hip when he was walking across a pad to the chicken coops and slipped on ice beneath snow and fell.  He was admitted to the hospital and may need surgery.

An employee was troubleshooting the installation of a tool (XT1000 - used in wafer semi conductor manufacture) when a door would not open. The employee tried to manipulate the door resulting in a right thumb tip amputation.
Employee stepped on something (possibly a plastic cap used for shipping) and fell on her hip. She was admitted to Capital Region in Jefferson City, Missouri with a broken hip.

On 2/5/15 an employee acting as part of a rapid response healthcare team was transferring a patient from the inpatient bed to a cart when the employee incurred a back strain. The employee was admitted and hospitalized for 3 days.
An employee was climbing off a trailer using the trailer ladder when he lost his grip and fell 8 to 10 feet.  He broke his left leg, left ankle, and right knee in the fall.
A worker had both hands amputated by a rotating auger while cleaning Mixer 1, in Tunnel 1, on the raw production side of the plant.

Employee was attempting to pull a ladder out of a manhole at a sewer lift station. The manhole hatch cover fell on the employee and knocked him down the hole. Employee fell approximately 20 feet to the ground below.
An employee was working on the center mac of the radial truck curing machine when he sustained 3rd degree burns to approximately 11 to 14% of the left side of his body.

Employee noticed that the cargo door of his assigned Long Life Vehicle snapped while unloading mail. He placed flat tubs (plastic containers that are used to carry mail) under the broken cargo door to hold the door up as he was unloading mail when he either hit the tub or the tub flipped out, causing the door to fall on his right hand. He severed his middle fingertip.
On or about February 5, 2015, an employee fell approximately 12 feet from an elevator pit ladder. The employee fractured his left leg and injured his back and right ankle.

Employee was lowering trash from the edge of the flat roof he was working on. He fell 11 feet 8 inches when the soffit he was standing on collapsed. He broke ribs, shattered an elbow, and cracked his pelvis.

A helper began raising the powered dock plate. While the dock plate was in motion, the injured employee walked onto it and shut the trailer door. He slipped, and got his legs stuck between the dock plate and the back of trailer. While he pulled up on the plate to get if off his legs, he told the helper to pull the truck out to free him.  When the truck was pulled forward, the plate snapped downward and severed the ends of the helper's left index and middle fingers.
Electrician working at a client site tripped on an electrical cord and hit his head. Employee was admitted to the hospital due to brain hemorrhaging.
An employee received an amputation to the left middle finger while using the patty machine within the meat department.
Employee slipped on ice in the parking garage and fell injuring a leg.
Employee discharged a nail gun. A nail became lodged in the left lower leg, requiring surgery to remove.
Employee crushed finger while making gowns on machine #25. Glue had gotten on the material and the employee was sprinkling powder onto the glue.  One finger was crushed and others were cut.
A home healthcare/personal care attendant was taking out the trash and tripped and fell due to an uneven driveway resulting in fractures that required hospitalization.
Employee was walking to work when he slipped on ice bruising his right hip.

An employee was working on an offshore barge and fell while trying to connect a hook to a lowered boom of a crane. The employee braced his fall with his hands, fracturing his right wrist. The employee was taken to the hospital by helicopter to receive treatment. A cast was placed on the employee's right wrist and he was kept overnight for observation.
On or about February 6, 2015 at 12:00pm, an employee's finger was caught in between two collars on a pipe while assisting in the lay down of 3 1/2" tubing coming out of the oil head.
At the end of her shift, the worker slipped on a patch of ice in the driveway. She fell, broke her ankle, and was hospitalized.

An employee was moving the forks of a forklift closer together, slightly raising the fork. He slipped as he began to push the fork, pinching the tip of his right middle finger between the fork and the forklift mast.
An employee slipped on ice, resulting in a broken hip.
Employee slipped on an icy surface and fell.

Employee dislocated his right ankle while stepping off of a rail car. Employee was sent to the hospital where they admitted him because his ankle kept popping out of place after they set it. They had to perform surgery on the ankle.
A maintenance employee suffered an injury to the right hand during maintenance operations of a wire cabling machine.  The employee lost the ring and pinky finger on his right hand.

Employee was using a crane to pick up windows weighing 250 pounds. Employee's fingertip got caught between a window and a shipping container. Employee suffered an amputation from the first knuckle (tip) of the pointer finger.

The worker was attempting to straighten a load of pallets that the forklift operator was placing on the delivery truck. The worker fell off the top of the pallets, hurting his back and breaking several bones.

An employee of Hebron Inc. delivered scrap cars to a salvage yard.  While unstrapping the restraints, at least two car logs dislodged from the scrap pile and rolled/slid, pinning the employee between the trailer and the car logs. The employee was hospitalized for injuries that included internal bleeding.
An employee fell while walking in the employee entrance and hit face on the wall.  The employee was hospitalized.
Employee was climbing down from the fixed ladder of a grain truck after adjusting a spout. The ladder broke, and he fell 5 feet and broke his pelvis.

An employee was delivering a cylinder of gas to a customer.  The cylinder was being moved with a cylinder cart.  As the employee was walking the cart and cylinder to the customer's door, he slipped in the snow.  His hand got caught between the cylinder and the concrete parking lot.  The employee crushed the tips of his index and middle finger on his right hand.  In-patient hospitalization was required for surgery on the fingers.
An employee received a partial right thumb amputation while strapping lumber on the dry chain.

The employee was cleaning the windshield of a semi-truck with the hood of the truck open.  He finished cleaning the windshield and went to step down when his wedding ring caught on the hood.  The weight of the employee's body and the ring being caught on the hood caused the hood to cut the employee's finger.  The finger was later amputated at the hospital.

An employee was polishing a shaft on a lathe  with an emry cloth when his hand became caught, pulling him into the lathe and injuring his right hand. He fractured the ring and pinky fingers on his right hand and sustained damage to the flesh as well.  His right pinky finger was amputated due to the damage.

On or about 2/6/2015, a temporary employee was moving a roll of paper to place it on a corner board machine.  The roll of paper fell, striking him in the left leg.  As a result of the employee's injury, he was hospitalized for more than 24 hours.

Worker was repairing an overhead door roller located in the shop. He set up an extension ladder against the wall of the building and climbed up. After he made the repair using his hands, he fell while descending the ladder. He landed on a water pump that was below and sustained multiple injuries to the right side of his body, including his right arm, knee cap, ribs, and cheek.  He also sustained a cranial injury due to the fall and suffered a concussion.

On or about 2/05/2015 at approximately 10:15 a.m., an employee was delivering merchandise to a customer. When the employee was placing a case of bottled soda on the hand truck, a couple of glass bottles fell to the ground and the employee was struck with glass fragments in his left eye. The employee was hospitalized overnight for glass extraction.
Employee was walking in an open area when a forklift weighing 26,000 pounds struck his right lower leg and rolled over the leg.
Employee was preparing his truck to do electrical work on a pole. When he turned around, he missed the stairs and fell to the ground.
Two employees sustained injuries to the right hands while changing the tires of a snow blower machine.
An employee suffered a severe injury to his right-hand ring finger while installing a belt on the number 7 dust collector.

Employee was clearing a jam on a hydraulic press. During the process, the hydraulic system activated, and the ram caught the employee's right wrist and pinched it against the inner frame. The employee fractured his right wrist.
Employee stepped on a metal pin, puncturing the right foot.
An employee injured his back when he slipped on wet/icy ground and fell  getting into his work truck.

Employee was sprayed with hot water while cleaning an inductor (a piece of filling equipment used to fill the containers of personal care products). The nozzle of the hose came loose and splashed the employee with the hot water, causing burns to the skin.
An employee was running the pneumatic press when the part that he was working shifted.  The space bar that he was using struck him in the head.
An employee was in a tree approximately 32 feet in the air, when he slipped and the chainsaw he was using cut his left forearm.

An employee was injured while working alongside the FLA Turnpike. The employee was working behind road barriers and was struck by a piece of flying metal debris that came off a motor vehicle that was passing by the worksite.

Employee was feeding a 6 by 8 ten gauge metal into a roller machine. The roller caught his gloved left hand and pulled it in, cutting off his left index finger and peeling the skin off the middle finger.

On or about 2/6/15 at approximately 3:25 p.m., a worker was operating metal roller equipment. The worker turned on the switch and began feeding the sheet metal into the roller. Once a piece of sheet metal is placed into the rollers the machine begins the process of rolling the sheet metal into a cylinder form. The worker then began feeding another piece of metal through the rollers. At the same time, he reached over and removed the previously formed cylinder. The worker's glove was caught by the roller, which pulled his hand into the machine. The machine crushed his right hand.
An employee fell and struck a mail sorting basket. The employee was hospitalized and treated for a collapsed lung.
An employee received second and third degree burns to his left foot when he stepped into a pan full of hot oil.
An employee was working on a twister machine, removing a package of yarn.  The yarn fell into the shaft and pulled her finger into the shaft, amputating the fingertip.
Employee was performing maintenance on the Sweed machine.  He opened the machine before turning it off and his hand became caught in the gears.
Employee dragged her foot on the carpet and it caused her to fall.
An employee was hospitalized with a broken foot due to a forklift tipping over.

The employee was in a personnel lift and the crane it was attached to was lifting it to another area of the ship. As it was moving, the employee put his hand out to move the basket from the ship and his finger was caught.
Employee slipped on ice and broke her leg above the ankle.

Employee was mixing baking dough when the batch of dough came out of the mixer striking the employee in the abdomen. Employee finished shift after being struck and went home for the night. Employee was experiencing abdominal pain and went to the hospital the following morning at approximately 2am. Employee was admitted for internal abdominal bleeding.

An employee had his left thumb crushed by the wheels of a semi trailer as he tried to avoid being run over. The employee was knocked to the ground and pulled into the wheel well of the trailer crushing his left hand and amputating his thumb. The employee also sustained injuries to the lower left side of his body.
Employee was mopping up spills and went to get a wet floor warning sign. He slipped on 2/7/15 at 1:13 AM, injuring his left hip.
Employee walking to front entrance slipped and fell, bruising vertebrae, resulting in hospital admission.
An employee was using a propane floor stripper. The employee started feeling ill and went to the hospital. Blood tests showed elevated carbon monoxide levels.

Worker left the bone saw running while getting more boxes of meat to cut. The blade caught his coat, pulled him in, and severed his right forearm. He was taken to UF Health Hospital in Gainesville, Florida to re-attach his forearm.
Employee was helping to troubleshoot an air valve.  While trying to isolate the valve, the valve closed, resulting in partial amputation of his left middle finger.
A material handler employee's foot was run over by a large aluminum air craft container.
Employee tripped on luggage in the doorway of a guest room, impacting with the floor, and hurting the left shoulder.

An employee was carrying a bucket of cleaning liquid through the facility when he tripped and fell. The impact allowed a splash of cleaner to make contact with his eyes, exposing them to corrosive chemicals.

A Walmart employee was using a tire balancing machine in the Tire Lube Express Area.  The machine was spinning a tire to balance. The employee reached in to flip the tire over to balance it and the tire slipped.  The employee tried to grab the tire, but it slipped and his hand was pulled into the machine.  The machine was still spinning at a high rate of speed. His hand got caught on the tire mount and rim.  His forefinger (ring finger) was amputated at the tip of finger and his middle finger was severely damaged.  He was taken to the hospital and admitted.
Employee sustained a broken rib while lifting a box at the facility. Employee was hospitalized.
Employee slipped on the ice leaving a client's home and broke her left ankle.

Employee was cutting bands from a group of slit coils.  The coils were on the turnstile arm.  They were not in a static position. When the last piece was cut, it fell off the turnstile and hit the employee.  The piece was approximately 60 inches long and weighed 2000 pounds.
Employee stepped off of excavation equipment and broke his knee.

Employee was pushing a tall, tin cart filled with dishes off the truck lift gate to the dock. An employee was on the loading dock helping maneuver the carts.  As the cart was pushed from the lift gate to the dock, it tipped forward and fell on the employee crushing his shins/feet.  He is currently in the hospital.

An employee was injured while operating a pallet jack in the store sort area of the warehouse. The employee's leg became caught between the pallet jack she was operating and other equipment. The employee was hospitalized.
On February 9, 2015, an employee slipped and fell while delivering mail at a residential home.
On 2/9/2015 at approximately 7:15 pm, an employee amputated the left middle finger (1st joint) with a belt and pulley on a wire bagging machine.
An employee suffered an amputation to the first knuckle of the left pinky finger, while attempting to clear a jam in a molding machine.
An employee was injured by forklift extensions when lifting a load of sheet metal.

Employee was operating a chop saw. Employee was clearing the trimmings from the point of operation. While he had his hand in the point of operation, the saw activated and the blade came up, amputating his right hand. The employee was taken to the hospital for re-attachment surgery.
Employee cut the tip of his finger with a knife when he was opening the plastic of a pallet.  He sustained a laceration to the middle finger on his right hand.
An employee slipped on a wet floor in the breakroom and fell sustaining a head injury and was hospitalized on 2/10/2015.

An employee was injured and hospitalized after stepping into a containment dike sump area.  The containment area is approximately 18 inches deep and is siphoned out of the sump with a steam siphon.  At the time of the incident, the siphon was plugged in, which resulted in steam being diverted back into the sump and the water being heated.  The employee was burned from about his left knee to his left foot.
Employee slipped on ice on the open grate steps by the wastewater facility. The employee's leg broke, and the employee required in-patient hospitalization and surgery.

An employee was working with the injection mold machine when a plastic part got stuck and his arm got caught in the machine.  The mold closed on his hand/arm, resulting in crushing injuries to his hand and lower arm.
Employee fell from a tractor trailer while offloading vehicles. Employee injured right shoulder, right side of head, and right ribs.

On 2/9/15, an employee who works for National L.S. Inc. was at a HEB Distribution Center in Houston, Texas.  The employee was about to begin his shift (6:30 am) to unload a truck for the distribution center.  At the time of the accident, the employee  was standing at the side of a Barrett double pallet jack trying to move the machine.  The machine was on and struck the employee, pinning him between the Barrett double pallet jack and another pallet jack next to the area.  The employee sustained a fractured pelvis.  The employee was hospitalized.
Employee was struck by a 12-inch pipe while it was being lowered into a three-foot deep trench, breaking his leg in two places above the ankle.
Worker was conducting re-roofing work on a two-story, split-level home without his personal fall protective equipment. He slipped, fell 10 feet to the ground, and hurt his tail bone.
Two employees were struck by a copper pipe when they went into a storage room to retrieve pipe. Employee #1 was treated for bruising and released; employee #2 was admitted for monitoring.
Employee was walking to car when leaving work and slipped and fell on ice in company parking lot. Employee suffered a broken leg.
On or about Monday, February 9, 2015, at 2:45 pm an employee was changing a transformer in a Merit Energy oil rig when he touched a hot wire injuring his head and left hand.
Employee was struck and run over by a tractor trailer truck.
Employee was reconnecting the battery on the forklift when he pinched his left pinky finger.

An employee was unloading decorative tile from a truck.  The employee slipped and fell backwards, striking his head on concrete.  The employee was transported to the hospital and admitted due to losing consciousness.
An employee received third degree burns on his back while using a plasma cutter to repair a trailer.
One employee was injured when he was caught between the mast and body of a forklift.

The employee was installing a gear box at the Diedeshiem machine tool station (used in cutting metals for making toilet valves). The employee was using a hydraulic jack to align the gear box on the motor of the machine. His hand got stuck between the gear box disc and the motor case. His left hand pinky finger was amputated and his ring finger was also injured.
Employee slipped on the water on the floor and fell resulting in pain in the right leg and left wrist. She was admitted to the hospital for surgery.
Employee fell while rolling a saw blade from the mill to the sharpening shed.
Employee was hospitalized after sustaining a laceration to the left wrist while using a saw.

An employee was removing a hand temper (compaction for dirt) out of a dump truck by lifting it with a backhoe bucket. His left ring finger was pinched between the tailgate of the dump truck and the hand temper when he grabbed the hand temper as it slipped and fell off the bucket. The employee suffered some bone loss (no amputation) and incurred 100 stiches.
Employee fell on ice in the parking lot and was hospitalized with a fractured ankle.

Employee was operating a wrap machine that wraps noodles in the production line.  Employee was running the film through and re-threading the film through the machine.  Employee had machine on manual cycle ( 1 bag every 5 seconds). His hand came in contact with the end sealer ripping his fingernail off.
Employee suffered amputation of the left index finger while operating a core machine.

An employee was injured while mounting a small tire.  The rim split and the tire struck the employee. The employee received lacerations to his face and fractures to his right wrist.  He was transported to Morristown Hospital and admitted for treatment.
Employee slipped and fell on the icy yard.
Two electricians came into contact with live parts which resulted in an arc explosion.

Employee was flushing radiator on a truck and when he started to loosen the radiator hose it blew off spraying the employee with hot water.  The employee suffered second degree burns on his right arm and right side.  Accident happened on 2/10/15, but the employee was not admitted to the hospital until 2/11/15.
An employee sustained a partial finger amputation after sticking a hand in a snow blower.

Employee was installing a TIW valve assembly for Blow Out Preventive (BOP) testing to get a pressure reading from the pipe. During the BOP process, the TIW assembly was sitting on top of the pipe when the pipe fell and struck the employee in the left foot causing lacerations.  Employee was Medevac'd to hospital to receive sutures in left foot and was kept overnight for observation.
An employee was hospitalized for a wrist injury after slipping on a floor that she was mopping.  Employee had surgery on her wrist.
Employee received an electrical shock to the right arm and right side of his body while leaning on a pole by the time clock inside the facility's sewing department.

Employee was working in the Wets Tool Area which has hydrofluoric acid (HF) in the wafer and tool area.  The employee was exposed to HF and was sent to the Burn Unit in Lehigh Valley Hospital in Allentown, PA.  The employee is scheduled for skin graft surgery.

At a delivery site branch, employee was unloading an 18-wheeler truck of milk into a delivery truck. The two trucks were parked next to each other and a ramp was landed between the two trucks' side doors. The employee was using the ramp to cross from one truck to another. While the employee was still standing on the ramp, the ramp fell from its holding place. The fall was approximately 4 feet. The employee was still standing when the ramp fell with him on it; however, after landing on the ground, the employee collapsed. Both of the employee's ankles were broken.  The employee was taken to the hospital and admitted.
An employee was cleaning a lap machine when the rag that he was using got caught in the rotation wheel.  The rag pulled his right hand and he lost the top of his right middle finger.
An employee's right forefinger was amputated at the tip when he got his hand pinched between two pieces of metal.
An employee was operating a hand-held grinder when it kicked back and caused a severe laceration on the side of his face and blindness in both eyes. The employee was hospitalized.
Employee suffered injury to his middle right finger when his hand got caught under a metal slide. He was admitted to the hospital overnight.
On or about 2/10/15, a worker fell from a stainless steel tank to the ground, approximately 9 feet below, and sustained multiple rib fractures.  He was hospitalized overnight.
Employee was hospitalized after the circular saw he was using slipped and cut his left thigh.
On February 10, 2015, an employee working in a classroom area stepped on toys. The employee fell and broke an arm resulting in hospitalization and surgery.
An employee was walking from his truck to the terminal during inclement weather and fell on ice, hitting his head. The employee was taken to the hospital and admitted.
Employee was maneuvering a piece of raw steel to drain residual coolant from the tube. The employee lost control of the material, causing his finger to get pinched between the material and rollers.

The employee saw that the material had pushed the home sensor and then pushed the material back manually, causing it to move forward again.  The material got stuck and at the same time pushed the employee's left hand into the clamp, causing an amputation of the left pinky finger, which left bone exposed.  The employee was transported to Unity Medical Center and admitted.
While riding a scissorlift, employee's face struck a doorway. Employee broke the jaw and was admitted for in-patient hospitalization at the University of Virginia Hospital.
An employee going to his car slipped on ice and broke his right leg. The employee went to the hospital and is awaiting surgery.
Employee hospitalized due to being struck by a bale of hay while loading it onto a flatbed trailer. Employee broke ribs, pelvis, and vertebrae.

An employee backed a tractor trailer into the delivery area of a customer store to unload soft drinks. The unloading area has a hydraulic lift platform with a lift gate on two sides because the receiving floor is at ground level, which is  4 feet lower than the trailer bed.  The controls for the platform ride up and down with the platform and are operated by delivery truck drivers.  The employee had finished unloading the product and was preparing to leave. He needed to slightly lower the platform to close the door on the back of his truck. He stood on an 18-inch-wide ledge and fell off. His jacket got caught on the control, which triggered the lift, and he was caught in a pinch point between the lift gate on the platform and the control panel. He suffered a puncture wound in the left groin, a broken pelvis, and a tear in his aorta.
Employee suffered a broken finger and a partial amputation on two separate fingers of the left hand while working at the tilt hoist in the planing mill.
An employee aboard the Gudrun Maersk fell approximately 18 feet off of a shipping container onto the deck of the ship. He was locking a cone on containers that were on the ship.
On February 25, 2015, an employee suffered an amputation of his left thumb to the first knuckle while operating the RAZ machine.

An employee working in the extrusion department was moving racking material with a crane when he pinched his left-hand, third fingertip between the hook and rack. The employee sustained a fingertip amputation and underwent out-patient surgery.
Employee was attempting to dislodge a dumpster that was frozen to the ground.  When the dumpster broke free, it rolled and pinched the employee's left pinky between the dumpster and a parked truck.

An employee was walking beside a crane, lost his balance, and slipped in the mud.  He couldn't get out of the way and was run over by the crane's wheels, damaging both legs. The employee was hospitalized; the extent of damage was unknown at the time of reporting.

Employees were opening a hatch at one of the salt water disposal tanks when a spark created a flash fire. The employee was burned in the flash fire and hospitalized. The other employees received minor skin burns and were examined and released the same day.
Employee received burns to the chest, face, and eyes when an Oxidizer machine containing propyl acetate and alcohol exploded.
Employee clearing trees for a gas/oil pipeline installation was pinned between two trees and broke a leg.
Employee slipped on ice in the hospital parking lot and fell, breaking her leg and ankle.
An employee suffered head injuries and lacerations after falling off of a truck while strapping down materials.

At the  Typhoon Lagoon Water, an employee was checking the slide for cracks or deformities when the employee slipped or tripped and fell. The employee fell forward and struck the right side of his face on the slide.
Employee fell down stairs while delivering mail to a customer, breaking his right upper leg.  Employee was admitted, kept overnight, and had surgery.

An employee was performing a utility locate near the intersection of Summit and Ridge Road in Eagleville, Pennsylvania.  While performing this work, the employee was struck by a car. The employee was taken to Paoli Hospital to be treated for fractures/contusions.

Employee was selecting orders while walking next to an electric pallet jack. The pallet jack drove onto the employee's left foot, pinning it between the pallet jack and the skid of produce in aisle 34. The employee was hospitalized due to multiple fractures to the left foot.

An employee was standing in a room next to the shaft alley of a boat on a dry dock where two employees were heating a steel coupling (shaft that holds the prop on the boat) using two rose buds with forced air and exhaust ventilation established. They were heating the coupling so it would expand and pop loose. After his shift ended, the employee called and reported difficulty breathing. He was admitted to the hospital where he was diagnosed with possible chemical pneumonia.
Employee fell 8 feet when he was transitioning from the ladder to the roof.

On February 26, 2015, an employee amputated a portion of his right middle finger to the first knuckle while arranging 600- to 800-pound I-beams by hand so the load could be picked up with the forklift.
An employee was injured when he slipped on ice and fell trying to push a company van.
Employee tripped over phone cords and was unable to ambulate afterwards.
An employee was hospitalized after falling approximately 18 inches from the first step of a step stool. The employee injured his hip and needed to be hospitalized.

Employee was standing on a pallet talking to another employee. When the employee tried to turn around, she lost her balance and fell to the warehouse floor. The employee injured her right hip and was hospitalized on 02/26/2015.
Employee using a Milwaukee Magna drill had his right index finger amputated at the second joint.
An employee was pulling a trailer in the Peterbilt Facility yard. The trailer turned sharply and the truck turned over.
While fighting a fire at the shop, employee received a burn to the left leg.
Employee slipped off a saw horse and fell resulting in a laceration to his arm that required stitches and an overnight stay at the hospital.
Employee slipped on the ice in the parking lot and fell backwards hitting his head.

Employee was cleaning insulator bushings on top of a de-energized transformer/regulator in preparation for tap switch testing. Upon energizing of control voltage for testing, employee received an electric shock.

Employee reached into the press #78 and his left index finger was severed at the second joint. The press has a pop up release which is activated after the cycle, the employee placed his hand while the pop up release was in operation catching the employee's hand between the part and the top of the press.
On 26 February 2015, an employee was installing drywall from a scissor lift approximately six feet from the ground. While working, the employee fell  off the edge of the scissor lift to the ground.
An employee was starting up a pump and a hose was not secured. As the employee tried to control the hose, he lost his balance and fell at the same level, hitting his head on the concrete.
Employee was operating a yard tractor, backing up a container; it jack-knifed and threw the operator off of the vehicle.

Employee was servicing an HVAC unit at a customer's facility. While disassembling the chiller, the employee stepped off the chiller barrel onto a pipe. The employee's foot slipped off the pipe causing him to fall approximately four feet resulting in a broken rib.
An employee was hospitalized for a possible concussion, after falling down some stairs.

At Sam's Club # 4998 in Lady Lake, Florida, an employee was injured when a forklift ran over his right foot, breaking three toes. The employee was helping to load carts when his foot was crushed by the forklift wheel.

A mobile conveyor was moved out of place for cleaning. An employee tripped over the angle iron bracing that remained on the floor. She fell forward, injuring her right arm and shoulder. She was transported to Lehigh Valley Hospital in Hazleton, then admitted to Lehigh Valley Hospital in Allentown when she experienced loss of feeling in her right hand.
Employee was putting a lock on the trailer door in the parking lot and slipped on ice, fell and broke the right ankle.

The employee was using a long board to push debris out of the conveyor, which was stopped up. The employee reached for a hand-hold and instead grabbed the conveyor. One of the 2' blocks of lumber and hit his thumb, resulting in an amputation.

On 2/26/2015, an employee was using a ladder to change a light bulb.  The employee fell from the ladder and was knocked unconscious.  The employee was hospitalized because of the injuries sustained in the fall.
Employee was burned by sulfuric acid and admitted to the hospital.

An employee had his fingertip amputated while using a rag to de-bur a piece of material coming out of a machine on the slitting line. The machine caught the rag and pulled it with the employee's finger.
On February 26, 2015, an employee suffered severe injuries while operating the A-line machine.  The employee's hand and arm were pulled into the pinch rollers during operation.
Employee was admitted to the hospital after dropping an iron casting on his foot. Employee sustained no broken bones, but foot is swollen and purple.
An employee working in the melting department was burned on the left leg when the exhaust line in the furnace loading pit exploded. The employee was admitted overnight to the hospital.
Employee was reporting for work, got out of the car, slipped on ice, fell and struck the back of the head. He was admitted to the hospital for a brain injury.
Employee was offloading steel from a truck when the load shifted, pinning his right arm between the steel. The employee did not break any bones and was admitted to the hospital.
An employee suffered a fractured left leg and was hospitalized due to being struck by an automated guided vehicle.
An employee fell in the parking lot due to ice on the walking surface.
Employee fell approximately 16 feet through a skylight to the ground inside the building.
While cleaning snow off of a roof, the employee fell through a skylight.
An employee amputated the very tip of his right-hand index finger while skinning a deer.
An employee performing maintenance on a palletizer slipped and fell backwards hitting his head on the concrete floor.

The employee was cleaning a part with a scotch brite pad when he attempted to clean the burrs out of a part while reversing the machine. The pad was caught and drawn into the machine, pulling in the employee's finger and amputating the nail end.
An employee was loading a ladder on the ladder rack of a truck. When the employee went to step down, his ring got caught on the rack and his finger was sliced open.
An employee stacking 115-pound metal skid pallets attempted to straighten a crooked one. Several pallets fell and struck the employee, resulting in a left leg fracture and ligament (MCL) damage.

The injured employee was helping chock pipe when the pipe started rolling. The employee ducked down; three pipes hit him in the back of the head and knocked him unconscious. He was transported and admitted to the hospital.

The injured employee was welding with his back to an overhead crane (fitter). The crane operator was using the crane to lift a 4'x3'x12"-wide beam assembly, but the crane was not centered over the load, causing the load to swing when lifted. The swinging beam assembly struck the bulkhead assembly behind the injured employee, causing the bulkhead assembly to fall over and hit the injured employee's body and legs.  The injured employee was hospitalized with a simple fracture in one ankle and a compound fracture in the other leg.
An employee was standing near a pot belly natural gas heater, and his clothing caught on fire.  The employee was admitted to the hospital.
An employee walking at the job site slipped on ice and suffered a spiral fracture of the right femur.

On February 27, 2015, an employee severely injured his finger while moving a 50-pound vise in the Rack Maintenance Area. The employee crushed the upper portion of the right pinky finger. Medical providers removed the untreatable portion of the finger between the first and second knuckle.

The employee was attempting to rework the alignment on a seam in a rolled metal cylinder when the spot welds broke. The metal struck the employee, resulting in a fractured left leg and numerous fractures to both feet.
An employee fell approximately 8 feet from a ladder while climbing to install satellite equipment. The employee broke both ankles and an index finger.
An employee was standing on top of a pallet while stocking shelves. The employee fell from the pallet to the ground and broke her hip. The employee was admitted to the hospital.
An employee was walking through the shop, tripped over a curb, and fell backwards.  He hit his head on the floor, sustaining a concussion and three fractured ribs.

Employee was polishing stem using two feet of polishing cloth when the cloth and the employee's glove got caught in the rotating stem. The employee's left hand was pulled into the stem, resulting in a left thumb amputation.

The employee was operating a 6-inch vacuum hose in a sump. The hose kicked back, knocking the employee to the floor. He broke three bones in his right ankle. The employee was hospitalized overnight and required surgery.
An employee was helping to remove reflective pavement markers when debris caused by the sledgehammer hitting the marker struck the employee's eye.  The injured employee was wearing safety glasses.

While disconnecting the chain from the connecting point of the hangar door, the employee's left pinky got caught between the chain and the door. The tip of the pinky and the top part of the nail came off.

An employee was delivering mail to a residence. The mailbox was mounted to the outside of a fence near a gate. A pit-bull/boxer mix that was inside of the fence jumped on the gate, causing it to open. When the dog attacked the employee, she put up her right hand and the dog bit it, resulting in broken bones. She was hospitalized.

The employee was driving the powered industrial truck, stacking product on the top of the third pallet. The employee stacked the pallet and put the forklift in reverse. The employee then placed the forklift in forward, assuming that the forks were still elevated. The forklift fell on its side, causing the employee to break an ankle.
An employee's fingertip was amputated in the workplace.
An employee working on a scoring machine amputated his right pointer finger up to the first knuckle.
An employee had the left index fingertip amputated while trying to clear a jam from the tissue paper convertor machine on February 27, 2015, at 2:00 pm.
An employee was struck by a piece of facade and hospitalized.
An employee was cutting siding into 2-inch strips using a circular saw on a saw horse. The strip started to buckle; the employee reached to grab it, cutting the palm at the finger joint.
An employee amputated his fingers while using a saw.

Employee was attempting to remove meat/fat particle from an auger with a stream of water. The employee then attempted to remove the particle with his hand. While attempting to remove the particle, the employee lost the middle finger on the left hand.
Mail carrier slipped on ice and fell breaking her left ankle. She was wearing spiked shoes at the time of the incident

The employee was helping a truck driver adjust the rear tandems on his tractor trailer.  The employee was under the trailer attempting to adjust the tandems when they slipped forward, pinning is left arm at the elbow area between the trailer and the tandem.  The employee was taken to Creighton University Hospital where doctors amputated the arm midway down his left bicep.
Employee inhaled muriatic acid.
Employee slipped on ice and fell while crossing the street. Employee broke two ribs and punctured a lung.
Employee fell at the jobsite trailer and sustained a leg fracture. The employee was admitted to the hospital.
A worker slipped on ice and fell walking from his mobile crane to the office.  He sustained a broken right ankle and was hospitalized for two nights.
An employee was attaching a compressor to a skid with a pneumatic impact driver. The employee's finger got caught in the driver, which tore off his fingertip; the injury did not involve the bone.

An employee pulled a car around for customers. The customers got in the car. The employee was preparing to close the door when a blue VW ran into him and the car, dragging him 90 feet and then running him over.

The employee helped finish installing deep foundation and began disassembling equipment at the site. While dismantling the crane, the employee used a hammer to knock a pin from a boom to disassemble it. The boom fell on the employee, resulting in an in-patient hospitalization and injuries to the wrist, both ankles, and the leg, as well as a possible back injury.
An employee was injured while unhooking a truck from the wrecker, requiring hospitalization.

An employee dismounted a powered industrial truck before it came to a complete stop. The employee's foot became wedged between the skate rail and was rolled onto by the vehicle, resulting in a crushed ankle.
Employee was walking outside near the engine room office at National Beef when he fell on the ice/snow and broke his tibia and fibula bones.
An employee was conducting a snowboarding class lesson on the ski slope when a customer on a snowboard collided with him, causing serious injuries.
An employee fell off of a ladder and struck their head on a concrete floor. The employee was hospitalized.
An employee fell while skiing and broke their tibia bone.
An employee was grooming a cat with a nail trimmer when the cat bit the employee. The employee was admitted to the hospital for an infection between the hand and index finger.
Employee was using a band saw in the commissary's butcher shop area to process meat for resale when he amputated the tip of his left thumb.
An employee performing roofing work fell approximately 12 feet.  He was laying down substrate at the time of the accident in preparation for the placement of roof shingles.

An employee was cleaning out a scrap box. The employee waved to the PIT operator to reverse. The operator started to reverse when his foot slipped. The PIT moved forward and pinned the employee between the scrap box and a guardrail.

An employee on a ladder was moving a box of meat from a storage rack when he twisted and reinjured his back. He fell approximately 2 feet and was admitted to the hospital for back treatment/possible surgery.
An employee was setting up a demo cart and preparing for a food demonstration. She turned and tripped on the rubber mat causing a fall that broke her hip.
On 3-1-15 at 12:30 pm, an employee operating a manual vegetable dicer amputated the left index fingertip. The fingertip was pinned and reattached.
An employee was inserting new pumps on the landing gear of an airplane. When the employee dismounted, he felt pain in his back.
On 3/1/15, an employee was struck by a passenger vehicle in a roadside work zone, resulting in an amputation.
An employee was draining condensate out of the treater line when a flash fire occurred, causing second degree burns.
An employee amputated approximately a quarter of an inch of a fingertip and also lost part of another fingertip on the same hand.
An employee amputated his fingertip while sharpening a chisel.
An employee's left ring finger broke due to being smashed between two parts of a dumper food processing machine. The employee was hospitalized and had surgery.
Employee slipped on ice and fell striking the head.
An employee working in the store was injured when a vehicle struck the building.
An employee got struck by an "I" beam and fell approximately 4 feet.

An employee was lifting a pipe into place with a hoist. The pipe came loose and caught his right hand between the pipe and a fusion machine. The pipe was rigged with a choker but not shackled.  The employee's right little finger was crushed and he was hospitalized.
An employee was working on a pipe with a breakout wrench when it slipped and severed his left ring fingertip.
An employee tripped and fell, striking his head against the corner of the house. He was admitted to hospital for head lacerations and overnight observation.
An employee engaged in roofing activities fell through the roof. He was transported and admitted to Kendall Regional Medical Center in Miami.
An employee was completely engulfed by silage at the entrance of an outdoor silage bunker. The employee sustained a spinal vertebra fracture, right hip fracture, and head laceration.
An employee walking to the break area slipped on mud and fell onto the concrete floor breaking his right femur.
An employee was emptying the contents of an aerosol can. The aerosol can ignited and burned the employee's hands, forearm, neck, and lower part of face.

An employee was cleaning the units on the second floor when he stepped on a loose platform close to the forklift and fell 10 feet to the ground. The employee was hospitalized with a broken right elbow and had surgery.
Employee was cleaning the press filter when he got pinned against a rack by a forklift.

An employee arrived at the facility early in the morning and was shoveling snow off of the front walk when he stepped on some ice. He tried to catch his fall, but the weight of his body broke the lower portion of his left leg. He was hospitalized.
The employee was leaving work. While boarding the shuttle, the employee missed a step and fell, fracturing her right clavicle.
An employee had delivered new appliances and was loading the old appliances onto the truck.  The employee's left middle finger caught in the tailgate, cutting through tendons and part of the bone.

An employee's right index fingertip was amputated on March 3, 2014. The employee was taking down operating room lights at OSU East Hospital. When the employee went to set the light down on the ground, a spring snapped on the light and caught the employee's finger.
An employee was assembling a metal part to a frame when the sheet metal dislodged and cut a tendon above the cut-resistance glove on his arm.

An employee was removing a pump from a roller machine. He took his gloves off to remove bolts. The 86-lb. pump slipped; he went to grab it, and his finger was sheered off between the pump and the frame of the machine.

An employee was on a 6-foot fiberglass stepladder, pulling wire through a conduit for a 24-volt DC fire alarm system. The employee fell off of the stepladder and suffered a head injury and broken rib.
Employee was hospitalized after cutting his finger while operating a water-jet cutting machine.
The driver of a front-end loader waste dump truck fell from the top of the truck to the pavement and was hospitalized with a broken neck.
Employee was pulling copper out of the copper shear when he felt pressure on his left thumb finger. His fingertip was cut when he tried to pull his thumb out.
Around 7:30 PM, an employee tripped over a rope and fell on his right arm. The employee complained about pain on his right elbow and was hospitalized.
A telescopic Kelly bar dropped on an employee's hand while he was digging a hole with an auger, crushing his left index finger.

An employee notified the press operator that he was ready for the press table to be lowered. As the table was lowering, the employee leaned over on the table; his first, right-hand finger got caught between the die strap and the table.

An employee was working from a step ladder to install cable at a bank when the ladder slipped out from underneath him due to snow and ice on the walkway. He broke his leg and was admitted to the hospital.

An employee slammed his left ring finger while attempting to close his truck's double doors.  An approximately 1/4" piece of his left fingertip was amputated (flesh only, not bone), and he sustained a minor fracture in the same fingertip.

An employee was placing plugs into tank bushings. The tester operator actuated the test sequence, causing the safety door to close while the employee's hand was in the door. The employee's left ring finger was amputated halfway down to the fingernail.
An employee shoveling snow outside of the facility slipped and hit his head.
An employee operating a tail stretcher machine sustained a partial finger amputation. The employee's fingers were not guarded and the left index fingertip was smashed.

On 3/02/2015, an employee was working in the freight sorting building on an outbound slide. At approximately 8:30 PM, the employee was sorting freight when she tripped on the edge of a floor mat that was slightly elevated, falling on her right hip. The employee was hospitalized and had surgery.
An employee's finger was amputated when a piece of unsecured plywood slid off of a forklift and smashed the left-hand pinky finger between two plywood stacks.
An employee driving a forklift collided with a second employee who was driving a forklift with a pallet attached to it. The employee injured the left foot.
An employee slipped on a wet floor and fell.
An employee was fitting plating when the plating shifted and crushed the third and fourth digits on the right hand. The employee was taken to the emergency room where pins were put in.
On or about March 02, 2015, an employee suffered multiple fractures to her right arm requiring hospitalization after being caught in a rolling conveyor.
An employee received burns to his face, head, and chest while refueling a motorhome with propane.
Employee's hand got caught between a belt and sprocket during startup operations. The employee was hospitalized.

The injured employee was standing halfway up a fold-down attic ladder, receiving instructions on what materials/equipment would be needed to fully repair the attic heater. While descending the ladder, the employee missed a step, fell, and fractured a vertebra in the thoracic area of the back.
On March 2, 2015, an employee entering his office from outdoors fell and fractured his hip.  The employee was hospitalized.
Employee's right ring finger was amputated by the blade on the meat-cutting machine.
Employee was walking into work in the parking lot and slipped on ice and fell striking the head.
An employee was attempting to get a ride on a sit-down forklift from another operator when he fell off the side of the forklift. The rear wheel ran over the injured employee's leg.
An employee was working on the third deck. As he was using a ladder to come down, he fell and sustained an injury.
Employee on the roof was checking a stand pipe and slipped and fell breaking a hip.

An employee was returning to the work area when a truck driver lost control, drove through the parking lot, and struck the building where the employee works. The employee was pinned under the truck and building debris.

An employee working on the production line between the window washer and the oven received a severe injury when the employee's arm was pulled into the conveyor system by the employee's smock waist strap.
Employee fell on ice while delivering mail, resulting in a broken leg and displaced ankle joint.
An employee was loading trash into the back of the garbage truck when he was struck by a drunk driver.
An employee was taking a Rhesus monkey out of the rig. She was unfastening the last head post when the monkey bit her right small finger.

Two large metal doors that swing inward/outward were being closed to perform high-pressure tests on the SB-BOP. The injured employee's left index finger's distal phalanx got pinched/stuck between the doors while closing them. The employee jerked the hand away and sustained an amputation (no bone removal) to the finger.
An employee was working in the edible cutting section using a conveyor fed belt saw. His thumb made contact with the saw blade, removing the tip of his left thumb halfway down the thumbnail.
Employee was in a car accident while delivering food.
Employee got his finger caught in a machine.
An employee climbing a ladder fell 12 feet and injured his right wrist and both ankles.

An employee was inspecting a tooling knife on a slitting machine. The employee fell into the machine when it was jogged forward. His left foot was degloved up to the ankle, and he broke numerous bones. He was hospitalized and required surgery.
An employee was injured on the harvest floor while opening shanks. The employee suffered a laceration to the right forearm and was hospitalized.
An employee was using a ladder, missed a step, fell, and fractured his leg.
The employee was salting the sidewalks and slipped on ice and fell resulting in a fracture.

An employee had just retrieved a full 30 lb. propane tank from storage and was walking and carrying the tank to place it on a forklift truck. The employee slipped on ice and fell breaking his fibula and tibia bones.
An employee was unloading a trailer using a forklift. While reversing the forklift, the employee struck the dock door, fracturing the left thumb.
Employee's left hand got caught in a conveyor belt and pulley while increasing the tension. The employee's left index finger was amputated.
An employee was shocked when he pushed the start button on a vibrator to shake material out of a bin. He fell back onto a 32-inch highway concrete barrier and hit his right shoulder and left cheek.

On 3/3/15, an employee slipped on ice in the parking lot and fell.  The employee was immediately taken for medical treatment where X-rays showed a broken right arm or humerus.  The employee was scheduled to see an Orthopedist on 3/4/15.  Following the appointment with the Orthopedist, the employee was admitted to the hospital for surgery on her broken humerus.
Employee slipped on ice in a customer's parking lot and fell resulting in two broken ribs and a punctured lung.
One employee fell and struck his head against a tree stump.

An employee slipped or tripped when bending over to pick up metal studs from the storage area.  The employee fell onto the pile of metal studs and received a laceration that resulted in a hospitalization and surgery to repair the tendon.
An employee was struck by falling blocks from a crane.
Employee fell approximately 4 four feet from the top of a precast concrete wall, injuring his head and fracturing his ribs.  Sleet was a contributing factor.
An employee was moving equipment when she tripped over equipment cord, hitting her face on a shelf.
While in the parking lot, the employee slipped on black ice and fell on her back resulting in skull fracture.
The injured employee's hair got caught in the unguarded belts of a die-cutting machine as he was making an adjustment to the machine. His hair and scalp were removed.
Molten metal spilled from a ladle onto an employee's left foot, causing burns and hospital admission.

An employee was cleaning a pump near the marination mix tank. She removed the piping but did not remove the cover and reached into the opening. She felt the sharpness of the impeller and quickly withdrew her hand. The distal portion of the third finger on the left hand was amputated.
A robotic arm pinned an employee's head to a CNC machine while he was performing maintenance work.
A worker was cutting steel tubing using a band saw. His right index finger was amputated by the blade.
An employee fell off of a ladder at a jobsite and was admitted to the hospital after sustaining broken ribs.

An employee was hanging a lashing bar on the aft end of the ship. The bar popped out of the corner and pinched the employee's right thumb between the railing and the lashing bar. The thumb tip was severed.
An employee slipped on ice, sustaining a concussion, broken right femur, and crushed knee.
An employee amputated the left index finger at the first knuckle while operating a Skilsaw to cut the end of a board.
A maintenance employee was using a drill press when their left pinky finger was caught in a slot on the work bench, resulting in a fingertip amputation.

Employee was walking between the garage and his truck, carrying an approximately 25 lb. cable reel. He slipped on the snow and fell.  He drove himself to the hospital, suffered a hernia and had surgery.

An employee was operating a shaper to mold pieces of wood when a piece of wood got thrown out of the shaper and caused the employee's fingers to make contact with the shaper knife. He lost the first digit of his ring finger, more than half of his middle finger, and his index fingertip to the bone on the right hand, requiring hospitalization.

A safe door closed on the employee's right middle finger. Her finger was bleeding, so she sat down on the chair by the safe. When she stood up, she fainted and fell forward, hitting her face on the computer console on the edge of the desk. She was discovered by a coworker on the floor. The employee broke her tooth. She was admitted to the hospital.
An employee was exposed to steam that contained sodium sulfate, tetrasodium pyrophosphate, and potassium hydroxide while working on an HVAC system in the basement/mechanical room of the hospital.
An employee was delivering a package when ice and snow fell from the roof and struck her. She sustained a fractured ankle, as well as rib and lung injuries, and was admitted to the hospital.
An employee, who was unloading a truck, slipped on ice, fell, struck his head, and was admitted to hospital.
The employee was traveling through the shop area in the dark to turn on the lights when she tripped over a lawnmower and fractured her left ankle.
An employee slipped on ice and fell suffering a broken wrist which required surgery.
Employee was walking between two buildings and slipped on a side walk and fell landing on her knee.
On March 4, 2015, an employee spreading ice melt slipped on ice and fractured his right ankle.

An employee was using a come-along while performing maintenance on the leaf springs of a bus. The come-along slipped out of position and struck the employee in the right temporal lobe area, resulting in a deep laceration and fractured skull.

On Monday, March 2, 2015, at approximately 7:00 pm, an employee was operating a blow molding machine. The employee reached past the guard, and the machine cycled and smashed four fingers on the employee's right hand. The employee sustained an amputation of the fourth digit, partial amputation of the fifth digit, and a full thickness burn to the right middle finger. The employee was admitted to the hospital.
An employee injured his wrist and head when he slipped on a three-rung ladder. He was admitted to the hospital and treated.
An employee sustained head injuries when he fell 54 inches off the back end of a conveyor load truck and landed on the concrete.

An employee fell from the third floor to the second floor when his foot got stuck on a pallet. He fell with the pallet to the second floor. He broke his femur and was admitted to the hospital and treated.
An employee amputated a fingertip while attaching a tandem trailer dolly to the first trailer's pintle hook.
An employee fell through the roof while inspecting the wood to see if it was rotten. He injured his lower lumbar.
An employee was prepping a recreational race course surface by side-slipping his skis.  The employee caught his downhill ski edge and fell, fracturing several ribs and rupturing his spleen.
An employee pushing the breakfast cart across the street from the church kitchen to the school slipped on ice and broke his left ankle, resulting in hospitalization and surgery.
An employee's finger was caught between two flange faces while manually positioning a portable pipe skid.
An employee suffered an amputation of his index fingertip when he tried to unjam the bagging machine.

An employee was using 2-inch, clear packaging tape to secure boxes on a pallet. He inhaled a small piece of the tape while cutting it by mouth, and the tape adhered to a portion of his mid-to-upper throat. He was admitted to the hospital and underwent treatment.

An employee carrying a pipe from the building slipped on black ice. The employee suffered multiple facial fractures, internal cranial bleeding, and loss of consciousness.
An employee was walking along the path when she slipped on ice and broke her arm. The injury resulted in a compound fracture, hospitalization, and surgery.

An employee was unloading fuel into a tank at a customer location. He was walking while offloading and talking with another employee when he lost consciousness.  A local bystander attempted CPR. Employee was taken to the hospital.
An employee fell off of a one-story metal roof, breaking multiple bones and requiring hospitalization.
An employee was using his finger to align the barrel of a gun while another employee applied pressure. The barrel slid into place, and the finger used to align the barrels was amputated.
An employee performing baton training received a rotator cuff tear and was admitted to the hospital.

An employee amputated his left thumb at the distal joint while using an overhead gantry crane. His thumb got caught in a pinch point between a metal plate weighing approximately 300 pounds and the lifting frame when a magnet holding the plate failed.

An employee operating a forklift was unable to stop the forklift from moving. His hand reached out of the cage to try to stop the lift. When that didn't work, he pulled his hand back in and realized it was injured.

An employee was using a rail mover to move three railcars. An employee on the ground was assisting him, and the two were communicating via radio. The employee on the ground became trapped between two of the railcars. He was taken to the hospital (Erie County Medical Center) with a non-displaced sacral fracture and torn cartilage in his pelvic area.
Employee fell down a single step coming out of a meeting and broke a hip.
An employee lost consciousness and fell on the same level onto a concrete floor, injuring his head. The employee was hospitalized.
A carpet roll fell from a forklift onto an employee in the warehouse. The employee injured his ribs, legs, and back and was hospitalized.
An employee was walking down the stairwell of the hospital parking ramp when she slipped on black ice and fell.
An employee was using a table saw to cut wood when his left thumb made contact with the saw blade, causing a partial amputation.
An employee's leg got caught between the pallet jack the employee was operating and the wall near the batter area.

Employees were building transmission power lines at the site location. They were changing out the cross arm of the power line structure and had the cross arms supported with two slings and a crane.  The injured employee removed the bolt that  held the cross arm onto the pole.  He rested his hand on the edge of the bucket he was working from; the cross arm slipped, landed on his hand in the sling, and pinched his finger between the cross arm and the bucket. His fingertip flesh was removed.

An employee's right ring finger was smashed between hydraulic tongs and a truck bed while running rods. The employee lost the finger from the nail to the end. The employee was transported to the hospital and treated.
An employee driving a cart (similar to a golf cart) struck an oncoming forklift, causing severe internal injuries.
An employee severely cut his finger while cutting meat with a band saw.
An employee was working on the back of a garbage truck and saw a piece of metal. When he reached in to retrieve it, his hand got caught in the compactor.

An employee passed a barricade in order to help seal an oil leak on the top cover plate of the transformer. While retrieving material that was dropped from the top of the transformer, the employee stepped into a hole in the grating and fell approximately 3 feet, landing on an I-beam.  The employee was admitted to a hospital and treated for broken ribs.
An employee was walking from a concrete sidewalk to a gravel area with a client. She tripped on gravel and rolled her left ankle, breaking it in three places. She was hospitalized and had surgery.

An employee was helping to install the top of a fiberglass well when the side wall of the well cracked and allowed the lifting strap to come loose. The tank then dropped, striking the employee and injuring his hip.
An employee fell approximately 3.5 to 4 feet from the bed of a shingle delivery truck to the ground and was hospitalized overnight.
An employee Injured her back while lifting a case of soda and was hospitalized overnight.
An employee was injured when he fell from a ladder. He was hospitalized with a ruptured spleen.
On March 12, 2015, an employee slipped on ice and fractured his arm while getting back into his truck at the company's distribution/storage facility.

When an employee disconnected a rinse hose connection from his truck, residual ammonium hydroxide (liquid ammonia) sprayed him in the face and got in his mouth. He was wearing chemical resistant gloves, goggles, and coveralls. His injuries include a minor burn to his lower lip and a 1/2-inch white patch on the tip of his tongue.
An employee fell approximately 15 feet from a deck being constructed and broke multiple bones.
An employee stood up from a chair, lost balance and/or stumbled on the carpet, and then fell.
Employee slipped on a patch of ice on the sidewalk while walking from his car to the building after arriving in the morning.

An employee was inspecting a C-130 aircraft using a 6-foot ladder. While descending the ladder, the employee missed the bottom rung and fell to the floor. The employee sustained a fracture to the right hip and received surgery later that evening.

An employee was setting a structure and was directing an excavator operator on where to dig a hole. He was standing between the bucket and a PCP (concrete) pipe. The operator could not see him behind the bucket. When the operator moved the bucket, the employee was pinned between the bucket and the pipe.
An employee was removing a washer/dryer combo from an apartment and bringing it down the stairs. The unit slipped and landed on the employee's right ankle, requiring surgery.
An employee suffered a broken pelvis when he fell from a machine.
An employee's finger was amputated while operating a service rig.
An employee carrying a ladder slipped and fell. The employee sustained injuries to his head.

An employee was spotting a tractor that was picking up equipment. The employee slipped, and the employee's hand was caught between the tractor and equipment. The hand was crushed and required surgery.
An employee was working in the tire shop when other employees heard an explosion. The employee was burned from the waist down and hospitalized.
