An employee was working on a valve that was suspended in the air with a threaded eye bolt. The eye bolt became unthreaded and the valve fell on the employee's right ring finger. The employee was hospitalized overnight.

An employee was unloading water heaters from a forklift. The heater box bottom was faulty and came loose, causing a shift in weight that resulted in the employee falling two stories. The employee's feet and ankles broke.

An employee was picking up some battery cells from the floor of the shop using a forklift. The battery cells were being secured by the employee, but the batteries slid off and his hand got caught between the battery and the floor. He was wearing gloves. The fleshy part of the finger was severed from the hand.
An employee cleaning equipment bumped against a heated roll and suffered burns to the forearm and stomach areas.
An employee experienced heat stress systems while providing waste service to household customers.
An employee was bitten on the wrist by a cat on Friday, 7-17-15, at 5:15 p.m. The wound later became infected and required hospitalization.
An employee sustained a back injury while lifting a 20- to 30-pound box from a cart and was hospitalized.

An employee was installing a Bliss Press by securing four tie bolts using a hydraulic torqueing method. One of the bolts blew apart and struck the employee in the left leg. The employee sustained a fracture to his left tibia.

On 7/17/15, an employee slipped on the bottom two steps while descending a ladder (billy jack stand). He used his right hand to catch his fall. He later experienced swelling on his right wrist and required surgery for a fractured wrist.

While wiring a ground bar in a 1940s electrical system (3 phase sub panel 277 volts AC), an employee contacted live parts. He suffered burns to his hands and arms after an arc blast, requiring hospitalization.
An employee went up a ladder to change a lightbulb, descended the ladder, walked a few steps, and then turned or twisted and heard a pop in the left knee.
An employee was using a handheld portable power drill to hang a job site sign when the drill bit hit his finger.
An employee experienced heat-related symptoms, including dizziness and low blood pressure.  He was hospitalized for dehydration, acute renal failure, rhabdomyolysis, and hypotension.
An employee lost control of his truck while trying to avoid a deer, ran off the highway, and struck a tree.
Employee was hospitalized for chemical burns after cleaning chemicals got on his clothing.

An employee was holding an extension ladder while a coworker was on it. The ladder slipped and the employee's wrist jammed, resulting in a broken wrist. The employee was hospitalized overnight and received surgery.
An employee was repairing an A/C unit. While performing maintenance, the unit started and cut the employee's right hand. He had surgery and was hospitalized overnight.
An employee fell off of a truck trailer and broke his leg. He was hospitalized overnight.
An employee slipped and fell.
After talking with a customer, an employee turned around and fell down on the floor, breaking her right tibia. She was hospitalized overnight for surgery.

An employee was standing on a step ladder to retrieve baking trays approximately 7 feet from ground level. While stepping down, she slipped off the ladder and broke her leg, requiring hospitalization.
An employee suffered heat exhaustion while working at the tire store on 7/18/15 and was hospitalized overnight.
An employee was struck by a mule pallet jack while attempting to get past it. His ankle got caught between the mule and a bollard. He fractured his ankle.
An employee was hospitalized for hydrogen sulfide exposure while pulling tank bottoms at an oil and gas waste disposal site.
An employee's thumb tip was amputated after getting stuck between rollers while threading the line.
An employee's foot got caught on a pallet in the lumber department; he fell and injured his left hip.

An employee was cleaning out the grinder for a spray dryer when a finger got caught in a pinch point between the fan blade and the opening to the fan blade housing. The employee sustained a left ring finger amputation.

On or about July 18, 2015, at approximately 8:10 a.m., an employee was dismounting an electric pallet jack in the warehouse.  After bringing the pallet jack to a full stop, she swung her leg out and struck an upright for a steel shelving unit, breaking a bone behind her knee. She was hospitalized.
An employee's finger got caught in a drill press, causing a partial amputation.
An employee was hospitalized after a 55-gallon drum ignited and fractured his leg while torch cutting.

On Saturday, July 18, 2015, around 9:00 a.m., an employee fell through the handrail system of an 8-feet-high platform to the ground while coming out of a grain bin during construction. He was hospitalized with a lacerated spleen.
An employee was struck by a forklift.

Employees were placing a 50-foot wood pole into the ground to support electrical lines. The line truck could not fit between the alleyway where the pole was to be placed. The injured employee was tasked with securing a bonding wire to the pole. He straddled the pole to about 12 feet to begin securing the grounding wire. As he stapled the wire, he lost his balance and fell onto the hard pavement/dirt surface. He was hospitalized and required surgery to repair his lower back.
A maintenance employee servicing a wheel abrading machine was hospitalized after breaking two of his right-hand fingers.
An employee's left-hand middle fingertip was amputated after getting caught between a large bearing housing and a tool rest.
An employee fell on a walking working surface, suffering fractures to the left wrist and knee.

An employee in the thermal forming department was troubleshooting a trim press when the employee sustained a left hand amputation. The equipment was not locked out and the guards were bypassed at the time of the incident.
An employee was hospitalized for severe dehydration.

While connecting an electrical volt meter to a 480V panel, an employee suffered first and second degree burns to the left hand. The employee was not wearing gloves at the time. The employee was hospitalized overnight for observation.

An employee was performing maintenance on a press. The employee was watching the motor and the belt of the press. He reached his left hand in to touch the belt and the belt engaged. His left middle finger was amputated by the belt and pulley.
An employee received third degree burns to the left hand due to steam from a vegetable cooker.

On July 19, at approximately 7:50 p.m., an employee was injured after stepping onto loose grating, which dislodged and allowed his leg to slip into an 18-inch deep trench. The employee received stitches and was later hospitalized for an infection.
An employee was heating up sealer on a seal coating sprayer. The employee lifted up the lid of the sealer container and a flame shot out, burning the employee's left hand and forearm.

On July 19, 2015, an employee was changing a bladder on an E5 tire press. While changing it, the rubber began to tear. He tried to grab the bottom ring on the bladder, and his right middle finger was partially amputated between the ring and the press.

An employee sustained severe injuries while operating a forklift with a clamp attachment. The forklift flipped, and the employee sustained a head concussion and a broken right hand, requiring hospitalization.

An employee was walking near a forklift holding a non-secure joint casing. The employee sustained a compound fracture to the leg when the joint casing rolled off the forklift tines and landed on the employee's leg.
While cleaning the rolls of a mill machine with a rag, an employee's hand got pulled into the rolls, amputating a finger.
An employee fell and fractured his shoulder. He was hospitalized.

An employee was operating a hydro blaster while cleaning a heat exchanger. As he exited a scaffold that was 15 to 20 feet in height, he slipped and fell through the ladder cage onto the concrete surface, injuring his lower back. He was hospitalized for surgery on his lower back.
An employee was cutting a steel pipe with a power grinder. The grinder kicked out and seriously cut the employee's leg.
While operating a table saw, an employee's glove got caught. The employee's hand was pulled into the blade, amputating 2/3 of the third left-hand finger.
An employee slipped on a wet spot in the showroom, fell, and fractured her hip. She was hospitalized and underwent surgery.

On July 20, 2015, an employee was climbing a fiberglass ladder to access a transformer when he was attacked by hornets.  While trying to quickly get off the ladder, he fell and broke his right arm and damaged his spleen.

An employee in the shop's face-frames department was operating a machine press that punches holes into cabinetry. As the clamping mechanism came down, it amputated her left-hand pinky finger. The employee required surgery.
An employee was holding a piece of lumber to cut it with a power saw when the saw kicked back and amputated the right pinky fingertip at the first knuckle.
An employee on a one-story roof was descending a ladder and fell 9 feet onto the asphalt ground, requiring hospitalization for severe bodily injuries.
An employee experienced an electrical shock and then fell from a platform.

Powdered product was being dispensed into a bag when the powder stopped coming out of the fill spout.  An employee reached up into the fill tube with his left hand/arm until his fingers reached the sliding gate valve, which opens/closes to start and stop the product flow. He pressed a button on a nearby solenoid valve with his right hand, opening the sliding gate valve in the fill tube. He then reached farther up in the fill tube and into the sliding gate valve. The injured employee was wearing a Nomex suit, face shield, and eye glasses at the time. The surface of this vat is at about waist level. The densest portion of the splash hit the injured employee in the groin, burned through the Nomex coveralls, and caused third-degree burns. An employee tried to clear a jammed part in a machine.  When he reached in, the part moved, pinching and amputating his fingertip.

On 7/31/2015, at approximately 7:30 a.m., an employee in the Intensive Care Unit (ICU) was helping a patient turn her body, so that the file film for x-ray preparation could be placed beneath the patient's body. The employee began to walk around the patient's bed when she tripped over IV tubing and fell to the floor. She sustained a right-leg femur bone fracture and bruised her face.

An employee was operating an auto-bend machine. She was inserting a piece of metal bar into the machine when her finger got caught in the machine. Her finger was smashed between the metal bar and the tubing, resulting in a right middle fingertip amputation.
An employee was exposed to molten iron when it poured on his foot.
An employee was stabbing a mud tool into casing when the employee's left-hand thumb was amputated just behind the thumb nail. The employee was hospitalized.
An employee was unloading a tractor from a trailer on a customer's property when the brakes disengaged and rolled on top of the employee. The employee sustained left shoulder and right knee injuries.
An employee re-aggravated a prior back injury while bending over to pick up an item, experiencing pain and falling to the floor. She was hospitalized.
A forklift backed over an employee's right foot, resulting in hospitalization.

At approximately 1:55 p.m., on 07/31/15, an employee was performing heat sealing on cotton bags.  A coworker dropped a cap onto the floor. The injured employee bent down to pick up the cap while placing her hand inside the platen press point of operation. She stepped on the guarded foot pedal, cycling the press onto her hand. She received second degree burns to her left hand, requiring hospitalization.

Two employees were involved in an accident on Friday, July 31, 2015. The employees were installing siding from a pump jack scaffolding when one of the support brackets came loose, causing the scaffolding to swing away from the structure. The employees fell to the ground and suffered multiple fractures, requiring hospitalization for treatment.

An employee was changing a shear's die using a hoist. The die became lodged by a piece of dowel. As the employee reached to check where it was stuck, the die dislodged while still under the tension of the hoist, causing the die to move upward and pinch his middle and ring fingers.  Approximately 1/8" of the employee's left middle finger was scraped.

An employee was overseeing a natural gas line repair contractor at the intersection of West Glen 7 North Monroe, Ridgewood, New Jersey. The employee experienced dizziness and light-headedness and was hospitalized for treatment of dehydration and low sodium.
An employee stepped up 6-1/2 inches to his work station and rolled his ankle, fracturing it and requiring hospitalization.
While grinding a gray iron cast, the casting got caught and pulled an employee's finger into the grinder. He sustained a partial amputation of the left-hand little finger.

An employee was using a handheld circular saw to rip cut a short piece of wood stock. The injured employee was positioned close behind the circular saw, helping to hold the short 2 X 6 wood stock.  The blade became bound, causing the circular saw to kick back. The blade struck and amputated the injured employee's left-hand thumb, requiring surgery.
An employee fell approximately 18 feet from a ladder. He was hospitalized with fractured ribs, a fractured clavicle, a collapsed lung, and numerous contusions and abrasions.

An employee was laying a culling table on its right side to access its underside. He tilted it towards himself by reaching across to the far side with his left hand and grasping the near side with his right hand. As he was laying it over, the top edge was approximately 6 inches from the floor when the table legs slipped. He lost control of the table, which fell and struck the floor. His fingertip got caught between the tabletop edge and floor and was amputated. He was hospitalized.
A Baker Boy Bake Shop, Inc., employee was hospitalized after receiving burns from hot water measuring approximately 180F while cleaning a conveyor oven.

An employee was on the back of a flatbed trailer inspecting a load for accuracy before the truck left the store for a delivery. The employee fell off the flatbed, struck his head upon landing, and was hospitalized.
While an employee operated a motorized pallet jack, his right pinky finger got caught and severed between the handle of the pallet jack and a metal machine.

A maintenance employee was getting a glass to rinse out his mouth after having some coffee. He immediately noticed the water tasted funny and spit out the water. A chemical sanitizer, pH+, used in the facility had back-flowed into the potable water lines and contaminated the drinking water. The employee's lips, inside of the mouth, and tongue were burned.

On 08/01/2015, at 0700 a.m., an employee was removing chilled iron from a cupola moat when he sustained burns to his hands, arms, and face. The employee drove the bucket loader into the moat after water was applied to hot sand, which caused steam to burn the employee.
An employee was walking his mail delivery route when he experienced heat stress symptoms. He was hospitalized and treated for heat exhaustion.
An employee operating heavy equipment was backing a unit into the trailer when the employee lost control of the unit. The employee was hospitalized with head, mouth, and nose injuries.
An employee working on the automated parcel bundle sorter machine fell to the floor after tripping on a piece of strapping material. The employee's left arm was injured, requiring hospitalization.
An employee was unloading a produce truck using a powered pallet jack. He backed into a parked forklift and his arm got caught between the forklift's arms. He amputated his right middle fingertip.
An employee working in the kitchen was walking past a co-worker who was working near a dish cart. The employee tripped over the co-worker's foot and fell, suffering a broken hip.

Schindler Elevator employees were removing a 17,000-pound escalator on a dolly. One of the employees tripped, causing him to knock the injured employee to the ground. The injured employee's pinky and right ring finger were then run over by the loaded dolly. The employee was hospitalized and had surgery.
An employee was removing a door. The door fell, striking him on the left side of his head.

An employee was landing in a jump spot. Upon landing, the employee ran into a coworker who was already on the ground and pulling his parachute in. The employee was hospitalized with C6 and C7 neck fractures.
An employee was lifting a 5-gallon oil container to empty it when he felt a pop. He was hospitalized with a collapsed lung.
While moving a scissor lift, an employee stepped onto the forks of another parked forklift. His foot got stuck on the forks and he fell, injuring his left hip socket.
An employee was called to help with an unruly patient. The patient became violent and hit the employee in the jaw, breaking both jaws and knocking out several teeth.
An employee was overcome by heat while welding building structure materials.
An employee tripped on a pallet of merchandise and broke her hip, requiring surgery.
An employee was cleaning a running tortilla conveyor belt when his left-hand, fifth finger got caught and partially amputated.
An employee was installing a kick panel on a forklift when his finger scraped along the top edge of the panel, cutting his fingertip. He was hospitalized for an amputation.
An employee's finger got pinched between a stationary forklift and a cart loaded with metal products. The finger was amputated.

On August 03, 2015, at approximately 4:00 p.m., an employee operating a forklift was loading a metal part onto a pallet. A second employee saw the part rolling and attempted to stop it with his foot. The pipe rolled off the pallet and his leg got caught and injured under the part.
A maintenance employee was working on a machine with a coworker when his right index finger got amputated in a rotating area.
An employee was setting a pumping unit using an impact hammer. The employee was hospitalized for heat stress.
An employee suffered a right index fingertip amputation while closing a parking gate.
An employee climbed up on to the roof to power wash a mounted air conditioning unit when he fell 7 or 8 feet and was hospitalized. No fall protection was worn at the time.
An employee working on the ground was disassembling the boom of a crane to add another section. A section of the boom landed on and fractured the employee's lower left leg.

An employee was troubleshooting a strapping machine and spraying WD-40 into it when his hand felt like it was going to sleep.  He rested his hand on the machine, and his ring and middle fingers were placed in a pinch point. He fractured two bones just below the nailbed, requiring surgery.
An employee broke a leg after stumbling over a die.
An employee was going up a ladder to the roof to perform tack welding. He had a safety harness on and was trying to tie from the ladder when he fell off.
An employee got caught between two steel forms, resulting in a broken leg and overnight hospitalization.
An employee was tracking a group of illegal aliens down river when he fell into a ground pit that was 15 feet deep, resulting in broken ribs and a punctured lung.
An employee was standing on the back of a box truck when he turned and fell off. The fall was approximately 42 inches. He hit his head and was hospitalized.

An employee was performing maintenance on a polishing machine. The employee was opening the plate/platform to get inside the machine to remove a part. After stepping in the open area of the machine, the employee felt a sharp pain/burning sensation in the right abdomen area. The employee suffered a hernia.

An employee was walking on a steel beam when his personal fall protection got hung up on a wire rope clip while anchored to a horizontal life line. He fell approximately 10 feet to the steel deck below and broke his leg.
An employee was cleaning out a mixer when his right thumb tip was amputated. The mixer was not turned off at the time.
An employee slipped on a scaffold ladder rung, lost his grip, and fell approximately 14 feet to the ground.

On or about August 3, 2015, an employee was painting from a step ladder that was positioned on a scaffold. The employee fell, breaking the orbital bone, nose, jaw, and both wrists. The employee was hospitalized.
On or about August 3, 2015, an employee was struck by a man lift while walking down an aisle.

On August 3, 2015, at approximately 8:48 a.m., an employee was operating a pie and tart press machine. The employee's hand reached into the machine, and his finger got squeezed between both plates during the pressing process. His fingertip was amputated.
An employee was using a handheld drill to drill into a part when the employee's glove caught the drill bit, amputating the left index fingertip.
An employee was filling a bend with hot water when the hot water spilled on him, causing serious burns.
An employee fell off an extension ladder.
An employee was hospitalized as a result of a left upper arm injury.
An employee was attempting to take a sample from the brownie blender. He lifted the lid of the blender. The lid came down and struck his right ring finger, amputating the fingertip.
An employee was walking across Route 367 and was struck by a motorist's SUV.
An employee climbed up a ladder to replace a faulty aerial drop at the mid-span connection point. He fell from the ladder and sustained a left forearm compound fracture.
An employee was hospitalized after being nauseated and throwing up from working outside in the sun for some time.
An employee got caught in the top plate of a shaper in the dovetail department. The employee was hospitalized for surgery on three left-hand fingers.
A Wood Products, Inc., employee was injured when his hand came into contact with a chop saw blade. The employee was hospitalized for nerve repair.
An employee was hospitalized due to heat-related symptoms.
An employee was walking up some steps and fell. During the fall, he cut his right bicep on a piece of metal.
On 8/3/15, at 10:00 a.m., an employee amputated the left thumb tip while cutting cabbage. The employee's cutting gloves had holes in them at the time.
On or about August 3, 2015, an employee suffered a fingertip (left ring) amputation after entering the point of operation of the hydraulic brake press during production.
An employee was picking up a mail tray on the bottom of a rack when the employee felt back pain.

Employee was in a boom lift elevated approximately 7 ft. high and was maneuvering the lift backwards when he became pinned between an aircraft wing and the lift.  The employee was hospitalized with trauma to his abdomen that required surgery.
An employee was working in the middle foundry molding area when he stepped in a hole and broke his left ankle.
An employee was unwrapping a pallet on the back of a truck. The employee slipped on the plastic, fell off the truck, and was injured, requiring hospitalization.

An employee was operating a PIT when he put his left hand down into the bracket that holds the battery. The employee's finger got caught and crushed between the battery and the bracket, resulting in a fingertip amputation.

On August 4, 2015, at approximately 7:45 a.m., an employee was starting to descend from a crane. As he bent down to grab the hand rail, he flexed his knee and his knee popped. He then called for help to get down from the crane.

An employee opened a rail car that contained sulfur and was possibly exposed to sulfuric acid vapors. The employee either jumped off the rail car or fell off the rail car.  The employee was not wearing fall protection or a respirator. The employee was taken to the hospital.
An employee was making adjustments on the paper feed of a printer when four fingers on his left hand were crushed to the second knuckle in the rollers. He was hospitalized.
A metal ladle struck an employee in the back, resulting in burns.  An interlock failed and the employee was not protected at the time.
An employee was photographing/documenting shipped items on the loading dock. The employee's foot got run over by a fork truck and the employee's leg also broke.
An employee operating a reach truck was trying to avoid a column. While trying to steer clear, she stuck her foot out and fractured her left leg.

An employee was moving a beam with a crane. He unhooked the beam and was lifting the hook when the hook caught the beam. The beam fell, striking him and breaking his right femur. He sustained a compound fracture to the right femur bone.
An employee was picking up a piece of equipment when a mechanism broke off and fell on the employee's lower right leg between the knee and foot.

An employee was working at a sub-station when he experienced cramps and fatigue from hot weather conditions. He was hospitalized for treatment.

An employee was using powered industrial equipment (picker) to retrieve products from a rack.  He was struck by another powered picker machine and his foot got caught between that picker and the rack. He sustained a laceration on the bottom of his big toe and second toe, and his big toe broke. He was hospitalized.
An employee's finger was partially amputated in the pinch point of a weave machine loom.
On or about August 4, 2015, an employee was staging coils with a crane. The two coils came together, pinching and amputating the employee's left middle finger.
An employee was hospitalized as a result of a right hand injury.
An employee was hospitalized due to an ankle fracture.

An employee was running a billet saw and attempted to clear a jam. His glove got caught and his hand was pulled into the saw blade, cutting his right middle finger and right thumb and requiring hospitalization.
An employee working in the store's back room twisted her ankle while pulling a cable from a two-way radio. She fractured her right ankle and was hospitalized.
An employee's foot was run over by an electric power jack and his toe was amputated.

An employee had a piece of weed eater cord tied around his left thumb while driving a golf cart. The weed eater string became entangled in the wheel of the golf cart, causing a partial amputation of his left thumb below the fingernail.
An employee was using a jointer to join two pieces of wood when his left hand slipped into the blade. His left ring finger was amputated.

On 8/4/15, at approximately 5:20 a.m., two employees were robbed while stopped at a Fuel Depot gas station to refuel their work vehicle. The first employee was shot three times in the stomach and the second employee was beaten up, suffering a fractured jaw, busted lip, and bruises all over his body. Both employees were hospitalized.
An employee was doing maintenance on a machine. His right index finger got caught and the fingertip was amputated.

An employee was standing on the floor of a trailer and pulling a piece of furniture. The employee lost his footing and fell to the floor of the trailer. He was unable to get back up and was hospitalized with a hip fracture.
During a baseball game, an employee was struck by a line drive to the head, suffering a skull fracture and dermal hematoma.
On or about August 4, 2015, an employee was moving a glass panel from one location to another when the panel slipped and landed on his legs.  He was hospitalized.

On or about August 4, 2015, an employee installing safety guard rails on the second floor of a building began to feel ill and experienced cramping. He was hospitalized overnight for heat-related illness.

An employee was walking on freshly lain concrete blocks when one of the blocks 
came loose. The employee fell, landing on his face and hitting a PVC pipe.
An employee sustained an amputation while operating a rolling stainless steel plate machine.

An employee was struck by an excavator and got pinned between a building column and the excavator. The employee sustained two broken ribs, a broken shoulder, a punctured lung, and a crushed artery in his right arm.
An employee was attempting to replace an air-conditioning louver on an inside duct when an air filtration unit fell and struck the employee's right pinky finger.
An employee was standing on a piece of equipment.  The drum that spools the cable caught his foot near his left little toe, and the toe was amputated.
An employee was retrieving a check from a safe in the manager's office when she closed the safe door on her right ring finger.  Her right ring fingertip was amputated.
An employee was loading a packaging machine when her pinky finger got pulled into the machine.
An employee was wrapping a load when a log rolled off the load and came down on top of him. The log hit his torso, cracking his ribs, puncturing his lung, and requiring hospitalization.

On 8/4/15, an employee riding the back of a waste collection truck operated the sweep blade control. The truck was in motion at the time. His foot got stuck between the sweep blade and the truck. Three left-foot toes were amputated.

An employee was entering warehouse through a pedestrian door. When the employee reached back to engage the warning buzzer, the door came back on the employee's hand, crushing the left middle finger and resulting in a subsequent amputation.
An employee was operating a lathe on 08/04/2015 when he got some of the shavings in his fingers. He attempted to remove the shavings himself. His finger became infected.

An employee was cutting metal rebar with a powered saw on the Staten Island Expressway (Exit 13) when the saw exploded, splashing gasoline onto the employee's legs. The gasoline caught fire, and the employee sustained third degree burns to the legs. The employee was hospitalized.

An employee was using a pedal-activated form roller. The employee was preparing to feed a piece of metal into the form roller, holding the metal above the machine when he inadvertently actuated the foot pedal. His glove got caught in the rollers, and his hand was pulled into the rollers.
An employee was lifting a coil with a hoist and chain when the coil fell on him.

An employee was mowing a lawn using a riding mower.  The employee was mowing on a hillside with wet grass when the mower began to slide down the hill.  The mower eventually contacted a parking curb and the employee was ejected from the mower. His left foot got caught under the mower deck and he sustained amputation injuries to the two small toes on his left foot.

An employee was inspecting a center pivot corner system to determine why the nozzles on the corner arm and overhang were not functioning properly. While navigating the corner arm platform, the platform tipped and caused the employee to fall to the ground and break his leg.
An employee was cleaning and lifting a screen on a vibrating conveyor when the screen fell, smashing and amputating her pinky finger.
An employee was closing off a pressure release valve when hot water sprayed his left arm and stomach.

A maintenance employee was troubleshooting a rotary valve for a pallet on the roof. While cleaning debris around the plug inside the fitting valve, the employee's finger was amputated by rotating blades. The unit was running at the time of the incident.

An employee fabricating highway signs was welding on a metal plate (approximately 530 pounds and 28"x33"x2") when the tack-welds gave way and the metal plate fell onto and crushed the employee's right leg.
An employee was cleaning the gluer rollers with a rag when his right hand got pulled into the rollers. The equipment was running at the time of the incident.
A chef was working when he started to feel fatigued. He was admitted to the hospital for dehydration.
An employee lost three right-hand fingertips in a pants press, which operates by foot pedal and closes on the pant leg.
An employee was struck by a vehicle in the driveway behind the quick lube service area.
On August 5, 2015, at approximately 4:00 p.m., an employee sustained a left index fingertip amputation when it was pinched between two crane pads that were being loaded by a crane.
An employee was holding a cat for a veterinary exam when the cat turned its head and bit into the employee's left-hand tendon between the index finger and thumb.  The employee required surgery.
While getting out of a tugger, a maintenance employee tripped over something, fell, and could not stand up. He broke his right femur just below the hip on his right side and was hospitalized.
An employee was overcome by heat stress while conducting oil-well servicing operations.
An employee was delivering parts when a shoe string got caught on a door stop at a customer's worksite. The employee tripped and fell, injuring the left knee.
On August 5, 2015, at approximately 12:00 p.m., an employee exited the cab of his crane and fell to the ground, fracturing his right hip. He was hospitalized.
An employee was descending a ladder after loading a high ceiling when he fell from the third rung to the floor, fracturing his vertebrae.
An employee got up to quickly address a patient's alarm. She tripped and fell, lacerating her head and fracturing her arm.
On or about July 7, a window clerk was handling an express mail package when she felt a pop in her neck. The employee went to hospital the next day for a neck injury.

An employee operating a lawnmower in the median was struck by a car that swerved into the median. He sustained injuries to his right leg and chest and experienced bleeding from his ears, requiring hospitalization.
An employee fell from a ladder, striking his head.

On August 5, 2015, at approximately 2:30 p.m., an employee was using plasma cutter to cut a length of 2-inch pipe. The pipe was on an automated table that uses rollers to move the pipe down the line and out of the building for offloading. Towards the end of the process, the employee pushed the pipe to speed up its exit from the building. His glove got caught by the roller, which pulled his arm in and trapped him between the roller and a metal bar. He fractured bones in his arm and hand that required surgery.
An employee fell off of an 8-foot ladder while installing metal canopy.  A beam fell, knocking the ladder out from under the employee who broke a rib and punctured a lung.
An employee working on electrical service started having cramps and was eventually hospitalized.

An employee was performing normal work duties doing a "meter run" when he started to feel badly and went to the Arnett office.  Employees/management at that location thought the employee was suffering from heat related issues and called an ambulance.  The employee was treated at the hospital for heat stress.
An employee was mopping a staircase with multiple sections and landings when he misstepped and fell onto the corner edge of the lower level step.
An employee was cutting a wood plank with a powered circular saw when the saw kicked back and amputated the right-hand middle fingertip.

An employee was pinning tubing together to skid the rig. The employee's hands were placed between the two pieces, and the left pinky and ring fingers got pinched. Both fingers were surgically amputated.

An employee was trying to remove a piece of geo-fabric while installing a 24-foot stormwater pipe when his hand got caught between two sections of the pipe. He partially amputated his left ring finger and lacerated his left middle finger.
An employee at a customer site injured her leg when she tripped and fell on customer-owned exercise equipment.
An employee carrying mail was hospitalized with heat-related illness.
An employee was leading a guided tour when a child started to fall. The employee stretched out to grab the falling child and broke his right ankle.

On August 5, 2015, at approximately 3:15 p.m., an employee was cutting meat on the power meat saw. He tried to cut some very thin steaks and lost his grip; his right thumb came into contact with the meat saw blade, and his right thumb tip was amputated.
An employee became ill from the heat on his delivery route. He was hospitalized for treatment.
An employee was cutting pork chops with a meat saw when the employee's right thumb sustained a partial amputation/severe tissue damage.
The last digit of an employee's right-hand index finger was amputated.
On August 5, an employee was cleaning floors and equipment when he hit his head walking underneath a conveyor. He experienced headaches and was eventually hospitalized with a brain blood clot.
An employee was moving cattle to a pen and went to split the cattle herd. The horse the employee was riding tripped and fell with the employee.
An employee amputated two fingers.
An employee was descending from a pole and got into a neutral position. He unclipped his belt and fell approximately 20 feet.

On 08/05/15 at 6:45 pm an employee was moving a steel I-beam with an overhead crane. The rigging caught the beam and the beam fell on the employee.  The employee was hospitalized with a broken right femur.
An employee's right hand got crushed when caught in the nip point between two rollers on a paper winder. The employee's middle and ring fingers were involved.
An employee's fingertip was amputated while cleaning a filler machine.

An employee was working as a laborer cleaning a new road that was done by the company. The employee walked over to a tree and passed out.  The employee was taken to the hospital and admitted for heat stroke.

On 8/5/15, at 7:30 a.m., a new employee received an employer-required vaccination for measles/mumps/rubella. Approximately 30 to 45 minutes after the injection, she experienced an allergic reaction; her neck swelled.  She was hospitalized and treated.

On August 6, 2015, an employee working on a gas leak inside of an excavation was bitten by an unknown insect on the right elbow. As the day continued the bite are became swollen and painful. The employee was admitted into the hospital. On August 10, 2015 a portion of the bite area was removed by doctors.
A worker was servicing a dock door that was out of track when he got his hand caught in the door cable.
An employee's foot was run over by a forklift after he stepped off of the lift resulting in a fractured fourth toe and broken pinky toe. The parking brake was not set on the lift.
One employee was hospitalized after a sample port on a sodium hydroxide line failed, showering the employee with sodium hydroxide at 190 degrees Fahrenheit.
An employee installing conduit for primary underground wire was hospitalized for heat stress.
A crane maintenance employee doing a cable inspection slipped and fell approximately 40 feet. The employee was not wearing PFAS.

The employee caught his arm between two trailer rear end frames while attempting to stop one from moving. He suffered a laceration and was admitted to the hospital. The laceration required surgery and there is nerve damage.

On August 06, 2015, at approximately 9:15 p.m. the team member was setting-up draw machine #5 (Morgan) for a double draw job (7/32 rod to W2.1). The process is to place the first draw under the bull block and the second draw on the upper section of the bull block. The machine was in jog mode while performing the task. An employee had the wire set on the bottom (first draw) and he was in the process of stringing the second draw. The employee noticed that the first bottom wrap was not in place. The employee stopped jogging and shook the wire with his right hand to locate the first wrap in place. While on this task, the employee stepped on the jog pedal as the wire snapped pulling his fingers against the block. The tip of his right middle and ring fingers were amputated. Employee was taken to the hospital where he was treated and released.
Employees were taking down sections of a grain elevator when an employee fell breaking a wrist and foot.
An employee was walking into a room. The materials he was carrying shifted and he tried to catch them.  The door slammed on his right index finger, amputating it from the nailbed.

An employee was trying to combine a low/empty jug of chemicals into a fuller jug of Sani King chemicals, unaware that he was mixing acid and chlorine.  The resulting odor caused him to suffer respiratory issues and he was admitted to a hospital.
An employee was struck by a PIV and admitted to the hospital.
An employee was setting a fan unit into position on a foundation plate when his fingertip became pinched between the two surfaces resulting in a fingertip amputation without bone loss.

An employee was working in the HT Unit changing a filter. The employee was sprayed in the face with hot water that could have been 100 degrees Celsius. The employee was taken to the hospital and treated for first degree burns to his face and neck.

A maintenance employee was chemically removing some walking lines from the floor of the overhaul area.  There was some paint thinner poured over the walking lines that were being removed.  The area was not quarantined off and the employee was walking across the area and slipped, fell, and broke his right ankle.

An employee was replacing corrugated roofing material. While descending from the roof, the employee lost his balance/footing and fell onto a concrete surface. The employee suffered a fractured skull and swelling to the brain.
An employee operating a table saw came into contact with the saw blade causing a finger amputation.
An employee was sanitizing a hospital room after a patient was discharged.  The employee slipped on cleaning solvent and landed on her left knee, breaking the knee cap.

Two employees were injured when a trailer dolly fell from the overhead rail.

A metal pipe line was plugged and the injured employee was attempting to remove the plug when the rotary valve positioned nearby was actuating and caught the air line the employee was holding pulling the gloves the employee was wearing into the actuating valve. The employee suffered a partial amputation (bone loss) of the right hand pointer finger up to the first joint.
Employer reported that an employee showed symptoms of heat illness (or kidney function illness) and was evaluated and hospitalized with IV fluids.

On 8/6/15, an employee fell in the kitchen.  Employee stated that he/she did not slip on anything and the floor was not wet.  The employee lost balance and fell.  The employee suffered a broken hip and a torn MCL in the right knee.
An employee rolled her ankle getting out of her car in the parking lot upon arriving to work fracturing it.
Employee was in the process of repositioning a vertical lift basket when his right pinky finger was contacted by a cable pulley. The employee went to the hospital were he was treated and released.
An employee, working as a winder, was threading a spool of high grade fishing line and got the right index finger caught up in the line amputating the tip.

On or about August 6, 2015 at approximately 8:16 am, a worker was cutting a piece of brick or cement when his saw got stuck.  Employee tried to remove the saw by pulling, when he was struck by it on the face.  Employee sustained cuts on the left side of his face near the mouth and jaw.

On August 6, 2015, an employee was trimming scrap boards with a chop saw at the end of his shift. He activated the foot pedal while his hand was removing boards.  The saw amputated the tips of his middle and ring fingers.  He was transported to the hospital where the doctor removed a portion of the bone in order to close the wound.
An employee fainted due to the heat and fell sustaining head and rib injuries.

He was caught in the machine and sustained extensive injuries to the right foot, burns to an arm and back and a possible broken neck.
An employee was in the break room having water, stepped on ice, slipped, and fell.  She was hospitalized with a broken left leg.
An employee amputated the pointer and index fingertips while operating the Macbee 30 draw machine.
Employee was hospitalized on August 7, 2015.  The employee complained of back injuries received from performing his work duties on August 6, 2015.

An employee was admitted to the hospital and treated for carbon monoxide poisoning while working on a school renovation worksite.

An employee pushed a cart through a doorway out of a walk-in oven.  The employee had his hands on the outside of the cart.  As the employee came around a corner, the cart cut the corner and pinched the employee's finger between the cart and the door jam.  The employee sustained an amputation to the tip of the left pinky finger.

An employee was assisting a visitor while standing on a curb. When he stepped off the curb, he rolled his ankle and fell onto the asphalt driveway, breaking his left femur.
An employee lost his balance and fell while working on a 10 foot ladder, breaking his left elbow, right wrist, and lacerating his forehead.
An employee was operating a rip saw that jammed up. The employee ran another board through the rip saw that kicked back and struck the employee in his right hip resulting in a fracture.
An employee was hospitalized after inhaling smoke from an A/C unit that began smoking. The strong burning odor caused respiratory issues for the employee.
The employee was conducting welding operations and after 2 hours of welding the employee started showing signs of heat stress.
The employee was cutting a sample valve using an unguarded grinder. There was a 6" blade installed on a 4" grinder. The employee cut his left index finger and shattered the bone.
An employee was operating a mower when he lost control. His right foot went under the deck and was struck by the blade resulting in lacerations and fractures.

An employee was exiting the restroom with her right hand placed on the door jamb.  As she closed the door behind her, her right middle finger was amputated at the base of the fingernail bed or distal joint.
The employee was shutting a trailer door and fell approximately two feet between the dock and the truck breaking her leg.
An employee's fingers were crushed in a brake press while operating the large drain pan brake press in the drain pan area resulting in a left hand finger amputation.
An employee was operating a pallet jack and ran into a conveyer that fell on the injured employee's left leg.
An employee was pulling a magnet off a door when she fell backwards and broke her hip.
On or about August 7, 2015, an employee fell more than 30 feet while removing trash from the roof edge.

An employee was working a piece of pre breaker when the pipe jammed.  The employee was cutting the pipe to release the jam when the safety gate struck the tip of the employee's third digit amputating the fingertip.
An employee slipped, breaking his left shin, while working on a concrete floor that was covered with a plastic cover.
While exiting an elevator, an employee tripped on weather stripping and fell to the ground resulting in injury to the head and spine requiring inpatient hospitalization.
An employee performing work in a confined space sustained an amputation of his left foot.
An employee was operating a Preform press (#1) when the pneumatic plate activated and severed the tip of the employee's finger.
An employee cleaned out a saw while the blade was still turning and the saw blade struck his fingers.

An employee working on a pedal operated resistance welder with no point-of-operation guarding received an amputation to the right hand index finger. The employee had a finger crushed between the electrodes.

On Friday, August 7, 2015, an employee suffered the loss of the fingertip and nail with exposed bone while repairing a band saw. The screw shaft fell out of the head rig (the guide system on the band saw).

An employee received burns to the hands and right foot while working near overhead power lines approximately 17 ft.  from side structures. The employee was carrying a 24 ft. aluminum bull float that contacted the overhead power lines.
An employee was hospitalized due to a left index finger amputation.
An employee fractured the little finger when a piece broke off from a 1-inch steel plate.
While unjamming boards on the planer mill, the employee had his third and fourth digit tips amputated on his right hand.
Employee was struck by a high pressure rigid line on a oil and gas production site and sustained non-life-threatening injuries.
On Friday August 7, 2015, an employee was assaulted by a patient in a locked unit and admitted to the hospital.

Employees were dismantling a concrete form when a forklift operator hit the corner of the concrete form and the boom holding the form tipped over onto a worker. The worker suffered three fractured ribs that punctured the kidney and liver.

The employee returned to the cement plant and was washing the back of the mixer truck with the cement hose.  The fold down ladder part fell down as the employee was rolling up the water hose striking the employee on the left hand and fracturing the left index finger.  The employee was taken to the hospital and admitted.
An employee amputated his left index fingertip including bone while repairing a metal punching machine. LOTO was not in place when the employee attempted to make the repair.
An employee was injured by a 40 foot tie rod that fell from a trackhoe excavator onto the employee's head and shoulders injuring two vertebrae in the neck and bruising the right shoulder.
A field inspector was struck by a DOT road sign when the strap holding the sign broke. The employee suffered a fractured right arm and a deep laceration to his right forearm including tendon damage.
In the meat department, an employee was injured while using the band saw to cut beef.  The injury resulted in partial amputation of the left index finger.
An employee fell off a ladder hitting his head on a concrete floor. The employee was hospitalized for a fractured skull and foot.
An employee was doing inventory in the Lawn and Garden area. A box fell and pushed her off a ladder. She fell three to four feet and fractured her knee.

An employee collapsed while pushing a shopping cart inside of the store.  The employee's head struck the ground causing bleeding and damage to the back of his skull.  Surgery was performed to relieve swelling.
An employee was struck by truck at the loading dock resulting in a broken pelvis.
A worker was travelling down a belted manlift in a grain silo.  The platform the worker was standing on shifted and the worker fell 15 feet to the concrete floor below.
An employee fell 15 feet off a walkway platform breaking his wrist and jaw resulting in hospitalization.

An employee was using a food processor in the Trim Room of the Salad Bar Department to slice/cut raw broccoli for a pasta salad. A piece of broccoli become lodged in the processor. The employee used the right hand to clear the jam resulting in the amputation of the right index, middle, and pinky fingers.

An employee was operating a diesel powered forklift to move cages off a truck. He exited the forklift and walked away to inspect the cages. Another employee entered the forklift to operate it, moved it forward, and struck and pinned the employee. The employee was struck on the right leg and hand. The employee suffered a right tib/fib fracture and right thumb and index finger fractures.
An employee suffered a soft tissue amputation to the left middle and ring fingers (distal) while operating a product wrapping machine.
An employee amputated the first joint of his left middle finger while performing maintenance on a lapper machine.

An employee was using needle nose pliers to close up the safety cable's compartment located underneath the right side of the aircraft by the aileron when he hurt the left side of his face and eye. The injured employee did not know what hit him. He was admitted to the hospital overnight for surgery.
A nurse was hospitalized with asthma symptoms after entering a room that had just been cleaned.

On August 9, 2015, at 11:30 pm, an employee was climbing a 5 foot fixed ladder attached to the reprocessing line when the employee slipped and fell to the concrete floor.  The employee suffered two broken bones in the lower right leg and was hospitalized for surgery.
An employee was opening a by-pass valve while working from an A-frame ladder. When the ladder slipped the employee fell approximately four to five feet fracturing the right femur.
Employee slipped and fell in the bathroom and suffered a head injury and a broken jaw.

An employee was taking off the access panel of the E Line Coagulation Tank to clean the excess solids out of it. As the employee was doing that the residuals (adjusted pH hot water 150-160 degrees Fahrenheit, liquid latex, and 93% sulfuric acid) splashed onto the employee.  The pH of the residuals was approximately 3.2. The employee received second degree burns down the right side of his body.  The employee was hospitalized.

The employee was supervising the outbound dock. A PIT operator passed by her towing two over the road (OTR) containers. As the PIT passed, the door of one of the OTRs came open and hit another OTR that was staged near where the employee was standing. That OTR struck the employee causing her to fall to the floor and fracture her hip.

An employee was climbing a fixed ladder with a cage inside of a containment unit when she lost her footing and subsequently lost her hand grip and fell approximately eight feet breaking her right ankle. She had surgery to repair the damage to her ankle.

An employee was performing maintenance on composer #1. After completing the maintenance task, the employee released the hood from the locked out position and engaged the pneumatics to lower the hood back into place via a lever system. Once this was done, the employee noticed a pair of pliers inside the machine. She placed her left hand on the edge of the machine and reached inside with her right hand to grab the pliers. At that time, the hood came down onto her hand, amputating her left pinky between the first and second knuckle.
An employee was working as a laborer guiding the forklift operator that was carrying a large piece of duct work when the material fell and struck the employee's right big toe.

On August 06, 2015, an employee was bitten on the left middle finger by an unknown source, assumed to be a spider. On August 08, 2015, the employee showed the employer his swollen finger and was sent to a doctor for treatment. On August 09, 2015, the employee's left arm had begun to swell. The employee went to the emergency room and was admitted to the hospital on August 09, 2015.
An employee's finger was amputated while changing a coupling on a drive shaft. The finger was pinched between an indexer sprocket and the cell chain.
A maintenance employee was working on a overhead crane from a ladder, installing a part.  The crane moved unexpectedly and the employee fell from the ladder fracturing his left leg.

An employee climbed a ladder to put a chain on the trim press. On the way up the ladder, the employee opened the electrical box of the trim press to make sure nothing was wrong with the electrical box. He did not close the door of the electrical box after checking it, but continued up the ladder to replace the chain. On the way down the ladder, after he changed the chain, the employee grazed the electrical box with his shoulder, shocking him and causing him to fall approximately six feet.
An employee was walking across the trailer yard (between the dispatch office and the fleet garage) and was struck by the yard horse (a 5th wheel tractor used to move trailers).
An employee was cleaning a deli meat slicer while the blade was still rotating and cut his finger on 8/8/15. The employee had surgery on 8/9/15.

Employees were moving pieces of rail into position with a backhoe to repair a section of damaged railroad. The injured employee was standing too close to another piece of railing when the backhoe operator set down another piece. His leg was pinched between the two pieces breaking it.

On August 10, 2015, an employee suffered an injury to his right great (big) toe when a coil that was sitting upright on the floor fell on its side and onto the employee's foot while the employee attempted to spin the coil. The coil was being moved from storage to production. At this time the employee has been hospitalized and it is unknown if a partial amputation will occur.
An employee fell while stepping off a curb in the mall parking lot.

An employee operating a planer in the planer mill received lacerations to two fingers on the left hand and a laceration to the left forearm resulting in hospitalization. A board became jammed and the employee tried to push the board through the planner when he was grabbed by the rollers resulting in injury.
An employee tripped while going down the stairs and fell down approximately 16 steps resulting in a separated shoulder, broken ribs, elbow and ankle.

An employee was unloading an auto clave, stepped off of a concrete auto plate located outside of the work platform, and fell approximately 18 inches into a condensate drain. The drain contained hot water at a temperature of 170 degrees. The employee sustained second degree burns.

An employee was severely burned (first and second degree burns) on his thigh and genital area by a lancing rod while attempting to remove slag on the cupola system. The lancing rod dropped and ignited a flame burning the employee.
An employee suffered a partial finger amputation while cleaning a machine drive belt. While jogging the machine, the cloth that the employee held pulled his hand into a pulley.
An employee lost his balance while working from an eight foot ladder. The employee was about to fall and jumped off the ladder instead, breaking both legs.

An employee was performing a fluid end replacement on a pump using an impact gun to remove pump suction manifold bolts. While loosening the bolts, the suction manifold fell ~6 inches catching employee's arms between the suction manifold and trail fender resulting in a contusion injury. The header weighs approximately 250-300 pounds.
An employee was changing a tractor tire in the field on 8/10/2015 when the tractor wheel and tire tipped over onto the employee breaking the radius and ulna in his left forearm.
An employee was using an emery cloth to hand polishing a part being rotated by a manual horizontal lathe. The cloth was caught by the rotating part which pulled the employee's arm into the machine.
An employee was chopping lettuce in the kitchen with a kitchen knife and amputated the tip of his left thumb.

A bladder assembly fell approximately 1 foot off the tip of a forklift and pinned an employee's left hand between the assembly and the press frame. The employee was hospitalized overnight for broken bones in the left hand.
An employee was using a Skilsaw to cut a post. The saw, which was guarded, kicked back and amputated the pinky, ring, and middle fingers of the employee's right hand.
On 8/10/15 a temporary employee operating a stand up fork truck was involved in an accident that resulted in a injury to the left hand requiring hospitalization.

An employee was working in a winding station and applying tape to a cardboard core (on a rotating spindle). The employee's gloved hand made contact with the double sided tape pulling her arm into the spindle. The employee sustained multiple fractures to the arm and ribs resulting in hospitalization.
An employee was working at the yard and was overcome by the heat. The employee suffered a heat illness, broken nose, and a laceration to his head.
An employee suffered a broken arm while jumping a fence on a residential property.

An employee was performing maintenance on a crane. He removed a pin that retained the dead end of the wire rope.  His finger entered the hole where the pin was and the rope shifted causing an amputation of his right index fingertip.
Employee contacted energized electrical wire. The breaker was not shut off at the time. The employee sustained an electrical shock resulting in hospitalization.

The employee showed up to work at 6:00 am.  At 6:15 am, the employee began sweating profusely.  The employee was placed on light duty and worked until approximately 2:30 pm. The employee was admitted to the hospital for dehydration at 7:00 pm.
The employee was operating a front end loader moving dirt.  The employee hit a pile of dirt and came to an immediate stop causing the door to slam on his left index fingertip.
An employee grabbed a metal frame from the floor and cut his right thumb. The employee was hospitalized for surgery on the thumb's tendon.

During pipeline construction and while stringing pipe, a track hoe operator was unloading pipe from a delivery truck when an employee walked behind the track hoe on the operator's blind side. The track hoe backed up onto the employee's left foot amputating it.
An employee stood up at her desk and tripped hitting her head on the right side of the desk and fracturing her femur as a result of the fall.  The employee was hospitalized.
A worker fell off an A-frame ladder into an adjacent elevator pit.

An employee was seriously injured after his arm was caught in a bulk palletizer machine in the finishing department.  The employee was hospitalized with multiple broken bones in the left arm and blood loss.
An employee was on a ladder hanging aerial service wire and was admitted to the hospital for heat related injuries.

An employee suffered a finger laceration on 7/29/2015 while cutting cheese with a cheese grater. The laceration became infected and on 8/11/15 the left index finger was partially amputated at the knuckle.
On or about August 11, 2015, an employee operating a meat band saw amputated the right index finger.
The employee was operating a forklift and hit a steel beam.  The employee's head struck the steel beam resulting in a fractured skull.
A forklift operator experienced severe dehydration and was hospitalized.

An employee was repairing the head stretcher on P2. The employee had electrical LOTO and one air hose removed. While connecting the second air hose, the shaft moved and amputated his left pinky finger down to the knuckle closest to the hand.
An employee was moving brush using a winch and caught a finger in the winch.
The employee was delivering packages and began to feel nauseous. He went to the cool zone, but was not able to cool down. He was hospitalized for heat exhaustion.
An employee's hand was injured while using a porta power hand held hydraulic press to change bushings on a truck. The employee's hand was pinched between the porta power and the truck frame.
An industrial power washer exploded sending an employee to the hospital for a fractured skull.
An employee was cleaning crumbs/crust from a catwalk and got her right hand caught in an unguarded chain and sprocket conveyor.  Her right hand was amputated during surgery.
An employee was standing in front of a forklift . A tote that was sitting on the forks came off and hit the employee, breaking his lower right leg.

An employee was struck in the shoulder by a falling piece of rebar breaking the collarbone. The rebar was ~42 feet long and weighed ~108 pounds. The rebar was being manually placed in a storage rack when it slipped and struck the employee.
An orange peel was left in a trash can.  An employee who was allergic to citrus came into contact with the orange peel and subsequently went into anaphylactic shock.

An employee was adjusting a belt on an energized conveyor with a wrench. The employee's hand slipped making contact and becoming entangled with the conveyor fracturing bones in his hand that required surgery.
An employee was injured in an silo explosion.

An employee was repairing a riding lawn mower positioned on a jack. The jack failed while the employee was under it cutting and crushing the employee's head.  The employee was transported to hospital and admitted for treatment.

A cold saw operator received an amputation to his right pinky fingertip (distal phalanx fracture). He placed a brass bar on top of the machine.  The bar was grabbed by the saw blade and pulled into the machine. The employee grabbed the end of the bar to pull it out while the machine was running, pinching his finger between the bar and a vise.
On 8/11/15, an employee was welding in a training booth when he began sweating heavily.  He was later hospitalized for heat exhaustion.

An employee was finishing up repairs to the 4DC Up Elevator. The employee proceeded to pull slack out of the drive chain.  After cleaning the teeth of the sprocket, the weight of the chain pinched the employee's finger between the chain and a sprocket resulting in the amputation of 3/8 inch of the tip of the left right finger. LOTO was used.

On 8/11/15 a rural mail carrier vehicle was struck by a township road work truck while delivering mail near an active construction zone. The employee sustained cervical and lumbar strain injuries requiring hospitalization.
On 8/10/15, an employee was sprayed with sulfuric acid while transferring acid from a railcar.

While adjusting the die on press brake #2524, an employee placed his fingers over the die. The back-gauge/positioner moved and caught the employee's finger between the die and the back-gauge/positioner.
The employee was on the third floor looking for access to the attic. The employee was looking up and stepped into the elevator shaft falling about 28 feet.

An employee was walking alongside a motorized aerial lift machine on unstable ground. The lift's tires sank into the ground causing it to tip over and strike the employee's left hand fracturing the wrist.
An employee fractured a femur while parachuting into a wild fire.
An employee suffered a hernia while moving appliances.
An employee was hospitalized for a foot injury after a wheel loader ran over his foot.
An employee had his fingertip amputated when his glove was caught in a chain.
An employee's fingertip was amputated after it got caught by the hold-downs on a shear.
During a training session, an employee hit a container and jumped off a standing toe buggy. The employee's ankle was caught between a cart and the toe buggy fracturing it.
An employee was folding a box and the lid flipped up causing her to fall backwards. She used her hand to catch her fall and fractured the left wrist.

An employee was on a ladder conducting telephone cable maintenance with the ladder resting against the telephone pole. The telephone cable broke and the employee fell 23 feet onto the concrete below resulting in broken ribs.
An employee had the tips of two fingers amputated when a sheet of steel fell on his left hand as he was feeding a roll former.
An employee fell approximately 4 feet while descending a 6 foot portable ladder stand. The employee got a leg caught during the fall and fractured it, requiring hospitalization and surgery.
An employee was stepping onto a forklift with his left foot when his foot slipped off the forklift. The employee twisted his ankle breaking it and his foot as he fell to the floor.
An employee received an electric shock while working on an air scrubber also known as a "smog hog." The employee was hospitalized for a night and received medical treatment.

An employee was working from a ladder putting up the angle iron at the garage door of a new home when the angle iron fell and struck the hose used for the spray painting operation performed by a different contractor on site. The employee came down off the ladder and attempted to stop the leaking paint which resulted in a laceration and latex paint being injected into his hand.
An employee was operating an engine lathe and was pulled into the lathe.

An employee was putting the rear gate on the state body truck when he turned and fell approximately 3-4 feet off the bed of the truck breaking his left hip and sustaining lacerations to his side, arm and leg.
On August 12, 2015, an employee suffered an amputation while performing a die change on a power press.

An employee was operating a press brake and caught his right hand in the die. His index fingertip (from nail base) was amputated, his two middle fingers were amputated from the main knuckle and re-attached, and his small finger was crushed and may be amputated.
An employee suffered an open fracture to the left foot when a coworker moved a pick car onto the employee's foot.
The employee stood on a pallet to look over a privacy fence. The pallet shifted and he fell off landing on his back and suffering a fracture in the lumbar region.
Two forklifts were backing up and collided.  One employee was taken to the ER with a back injury and was admitted.

An employee was climbing the newly installed wooden power line pole to help another employee who was working out of the aerial lift bucket move the 4800 V power line from the old wooden power line pole to the new one.  In the process, the injured employee contacted the live 4800v power line on the top of his right shoulder.  

The poles are approximately 45 feet long but once installed they are 35 feet high because 10 feet are in the ground.
As an employee was moving a B-pillar to the rack by hand, a second employee was moving a B-pillar off the line by hand and struck the first employee in the arm causing a laceration to the left bicep.

An employee was stacking boxes on a pallet. The employee struck his leg on a box containing product. After a half hour, the employee's leg began to swell and he was taken to the hospital. The employee was diagnosed as having a blood clot and was hospitalized overnight. The employee had surgery the next day.

Two employees were preparing to load luggage onto a plane with a belt loader. When one of the employees turned the loader on it malfunctioned. The loader jumped forward smashing the other employee between the loader and the plane resulting in fractured ribs and a jaw fracture in two places.
An employee was moving a piece of switch gear in the electrical building when it tipped and pinched his finger between the switch gear and the floor.
An employee received 2nd degree burns on 27% of his body from contact with hot water when his safety vest caught a valve handle that opened while inspecting a heat exchanger.
An employee fell off the back of a local delivery truck and broke his ankle, requiring surgery.
An employee had a finger crushed and later amputated.
An employee fell and was hospitalized.

On 8/12/2015 an employee who was delivering pavement stones suffered a fractured jaw. The industrial truck that he was operating tipped over while handling a load. The employee was wearing a seat belt and upon the forklift making side impact with the ground the employee suffered a fractured jaw. He was admitted to the hospital for surgery.

An employee was filling up the tire of a combine with an air compressor. The tire exploded and threw the employee approximately 16 feet onto the concrete floor.  The employee sustained three broken ribs.

An employee finished installing switches. While cleaning up and removing the rubber cover up used to protect from inadvertent contact, he touched the wire with more than 50 volts, resulting in 1st, 2nd, and 3rd degree burns to both arms.
An employee was cleaning the blades of a lawn mower. The mower jumped and severed four fingers on his left hand.
On or about August 12, 2015, an employee fell/collapsed within the break room area and received a hip injury that resulted in hospitalization and surgery.

An employee was attempting to repair a chain conveyor that pulls fence posts from one area of the facility to another. The employee used the emergency stop to shut the conveyor down. The machine wasn't locked out and tagged. At some point another employee turned the conveyor back on while the maintenance employee still had his hand on the conveyor chain. The employee lost his whole middle finger and the tip of his left pointer finger.
An employee working in the elevator shaft suffered a laceration to his elbow when the elevator suddenly moved and the employee's elbow came into contact with a metal bracket in the shaft.
An employee was replacing a flat tire on a flat-bed trailer when the jack supporting the trailer slipped. The trailer's fender came down on his left thumb-tip.
On 8/12/15, a temporary worker sustained an amputation of the tip of his right middle finger while operating a table saw.
An employee was picking up trash in the parking lot when her knee gave out and she fell fracturing the left leg in two places and dislocating the ankle.

An employee stood in a 32 inch deep trench with 24 inch concrete pipe while directing the heavy equipment operator. The employee was caught between the equipment bucket that was cleaning out dirt and the pipe.

The employee was walking down the corridor near the break room when her shoe caught on the floor causing her to fall and break her left hip.  There was no carpet on the floor or anything else to contribute to the fall.

An employee was wiring field mass meters by the flare when he started feeling the effects of heat related illness. The employee was working with another employee at the time of the incident.  The paramedics were called and the employee was transported to the hospital.
An employee lost control of the brake handle during rig down operations and it struck him in the jaw.
A crew was trimming tree limbs away from power lines. An employee got too close to the power lines and the current arced from the wire onto the employee whose shirt caught fire and burned his back.
An employee was standing on a ladder 16' from the ground.  He reached to the left to drill into the side of the house and the ladder fell to the right.
A forklift driver was driving a forklift and dropped his clipboard onto the floor.  He attempted to pick up the clipboard and as he leaned over the side of the lift he struck his head on a pole.
An employee suffered a fingertip amputation to the left middle finger while performing maintenance on a Bobcat.
A tow truck hook broke off the tow truck and struck a passing employee on the side breaking ribs and bruising the shoulder.
A greeter tripped on a rug and fell resulting in a left hip fracture.

The employee was in a front end loader attempting to lift a railroad tie.  She lost her grip on the railroad tie and it fell striking her right hand, middle finger on the bucket blade. Her right middle fingertip was amputated.
The employee was struck by a pulley system buckle that snapped and struck his leg. The injury required inpatient hospitalization and surgery.

An employee was getting into the side of a company van to sit on the floor to go to lunch. The employee touched a conduit that was stacked in the van, causing it to shift onto his hand and amputate his right index fingertip.
An employee was climbing the stairs leading into a customer's mobile home to deliver a mattress set. The employee tripped and fell, breaking the right hip.

Two employees were moving a pallet with a manual pallet jack when a piece of the wooden pallet broke. While one of the employee's reached down to grab the piece of wood, the other employee lowered the pallet catching the injured employee's left middle finger. The left middle fingertip was amputated and surgically reattached.
An employee was stacking pieces of granite about 4-feet high when the stack became top heavy and fell, crushing his left foot.

On 8/13/15, an employee was operating a spooling machine when their left-hand glove got caught on a cable and was drawn into an in-running roller nip point. The employee's left ring fingertip was amputated.
While conducting a routine valve cleaning operation, the employee inserted his finger into the valve body then activated the valve causing the ball valve to sever the tip of his finger.
An employee was scalded on the face, chest, and legs by steam and juice.
On or about August 13, 2015, an employee was struck by a forklift in the warehouse. The forklift crushed the employee's foot and ankle.

1) An employee was smoothing a screen under a heat bar as it descended. The bar came down on his hands and trapped them. He was able to free his left hand, but had to rip his right hand from his glove, amputating his middle fingertip and exposing the bone. 2) An employee was hitting a spike with a hammer. An employee was walking around equipment to lock it out when he tripped on the bottom of a guardrail and fell into the guardrail post, fracturing his ribs and puncturing a lung.

On August 13, 2015, at 2:30 p.m., an employee was cutting tree branches from a ladder while using a chain saw. The employee fell from the ladder and suffered multiple injuries to the hands, as well as broken ribs.  The employee was hospitalized for treatment.
An employee reached into an open trench to straighten some conduit and was bitten on the left-hand finger by a venomous snake.

An employee was working the night shift on the PA Turnpike, moving traffic signs for the blacktopping crew. The employee climbed over the jersey barrier where a bridge was demolished so he could retrieve personal items. The employee fell approximately 15 feet off the bridge onto Meetinghouse Road, fracturing the foot and ankle.
An employee's right-hand pinky fingertip was amputated while working on a screw conveyor.

On or about August 13, 2015, an employee was painting an elevator door. She got the door key to open the door. As she pushed the heavy door, it opened, and she fell 20 to 25 feet to the bottom of the elevator shaft, suffering sprains and strains. No fall protection or lockout protection was used at the time.
An employee was cleaning the ravioli former when the machine started unexpectedly. His right hand got caught in the paddles, and half of his ring finger was crushed.

On 8/13/2015, at approximately 10:00 a.m., an employee was installing electrical insulation on powerlines when a pin broke as he was coming down inside the bucket of a boom truck. He fell and hit the ground while still inside the bucket, breaking his ribs and injuring his right ankle.

On August 13, 2015, an employee was operating an overhead crane to move a steel beam that was approximately 4' by 15' and weighed 4,000 pounds. The beam was sitting in the I position and the employee was using beam clamps to move the beam to horses. The employee's right middle finger got caught between the beam clamp and the beam flange. The top portion of the employee's finger was sheared and had to be surgically amputated.
An employee suffered heat exhaustion while prepping a boat for painting. He was hospitalized overnight.

Employee was cutting grass on right side of road edge with a weed whacker. A vehicle that was merging onto the parkway struck the employee on the right side. The employee suffered injuries to his right elbow, right shoulder and head.

An employee was bringing a steel plate down onto a pillow block. While he was adjusting a piece of sheet metal, the block turned and pinched his finger between the block and plate, amputating his left index fingertip (part of nail).
An employee was hospitalized after an electrical flash occurred during an operation to change a wooden beam to a concrete beam.

A maintenance mechanic was drilling into a conveyor roller and a chromate chemical sealer sprayed out, ignited, and burned his face and arms. He was wearing safety glasses and was admitted to the hospital for 2nd and 3rd degree burns.
