He was leaning up and into the chipper to feel for vibration and his fingers got caught in the blades before the wheel had come to a complete stop amputating the fat pad and the fourth left fingertip.

An employee was attempting to start the commercial riding lawn mower in the manual mode.  While starting the mower, the employee's got caught in the pulleys. Half the index finger was amputated and the middle and ring fingers were amputated to the first joint.

An employee was performing maintenance work on a slide gate and chute in the head house of the elevator when he was exposed to some out of condition grain.  The employee began experiencing breathing problems, which resulted in hospitalization.
An employee was repairing an industrial fan and contacted the moving fan blades and suffered the amputation of the right index finger and a broken right thumb.

An employee was operating a brake press to bend a piece of metal. His finger was pinched on the deck of the press resulting in the amputation of the left ring finger just above the finger nail. It was reattached by a surgeon.
An employee was moving dirt with a skid-steer when it contacted a hard object. The employee's left leg got caught in the bucket resulting in a facture requiring inpatient hospitalization.
An employee amputated the right hand index, middle and ring fingers while running a compound mitre saw.
An employee lost his balance and fell in the parking lot, breaking his hip.

On or about August 28, 2015, an employee was injured while loading dollies onto a truck.  The dollies became lodged on the lift gate and the employee lost part of his left middle finger trying to move the dollies.
An employee was struck by a motor vehicle while working in a highway construction zone.  Surgery was performed to relieve pressure/fluid on the brain.
An employee was operating a roll-off truck trying to load a container onto the truck when it dropped on and crushed his foot.
An employee injured his scrotum when he fell approximately six feet off a ladder and landed on rebar.

An employee was pushing three pieces of lumber directly into the in feed conveyor of a gang saw and cut his left index and middle fingers. The left index figure was amputated just below the nail while the left middle finger was amputated at the first joint.
An employee stepped on a loose stone at the jobsite, rolled an ankle, and fell bruising a hip.

An employee was gluing a piece under a bathroom sink when the sink fell. The employee stood up and attempted to step over the broken pieces, which cut through his sneakers and cut the bottom of his foot.

An employee was using a meat grinder. He turned the machine off and reached up under the guard and into die because he thought meat was stuck in the die.  The blade hadn't completely stopped and his finger was amputated just above the cuticle.
An employee was on a ladder cutting an overhead beam. The ceiling beam collapsed and struck the employee, causing him to fall off and sustain a rib injury.
An employee was driving a flat bed truck and pulled over to adjust and secure the load (bales of film). The bales of film rolled on top of the employee breaking his femur and dislocated his hip.
An employee was unloading panels of windows from one cart to another. The glass sheets got stuck together and fell on the employee, severely cutting the employee's right forearm.

An employee changing filters on a filter system connected to a grinding unit dropped one of the filters into the filter unit. The impact inside the unit created a spark that ignited the aluminum dust, causing an aluminum dust deflagration. A fire ball discharged from the filter unit, contacting and causing second degree burns to the employee's hands.
An employee was sandblasting structural steel. He was using supply air from an air compressor when he felt lightheaded. He was hospitalized for carbon monoxide exposure.
An employee amputated a finger while rigging material. The rigging material slipped and the employee's finger got caught between the material and the steel beam.

An employee was climbing off of a carpenter's bracket scaffold into a second-story window. He missed the window sill, hung from the scaffold decking, and fell to the ground. He suffered internal bleeding and was hospitalized. A personal fall arrest system was not worn at the time.

On August 28, 2015, at approximately 6:45pm, while performing maintenance on a machine, another employee activated the machine after receiving verbal confirmation from the mechanic to go ahead. The maintenance mechanic suffered the amputation of his left thumb after it was pinched between a table and material near the entry end of the cap line.
An employee was trimming palm branches from an aerial lift/truck when the bucket contacted a 7200V power line. The employee sustained electrical burns on his back and was hospitalized.
An employee's foot got caught in the bottom of a rolling 32-gallon trash can. She fell face first onto the floor, breaking her nose and dentures. She was hospitalized for stitches and a nose cast.
An employee fell from the lookout tower outer balcony to the ground, fracturing their back, ribs, and skull.

On August 29, 2015, at approximately 5:00 p.m., an employee was unloading material using a built-in hydraulic lift gate attached to the rear of the delivery truck. The material fell on and broke the employee's pelvis.
An employee was carrying hot water into the freezer to remove ice. The employee slipped on ice, and the hot water spilled on the employee, causing burns to the face, neck, arms, and legs.
An employee was removing finished material from the machine when he tripped on the hoist hook on the floor. He broke his right hip.
An employee was closing the store. The store was robbed, and the employee was shot in both legs.

An employee was working on an oil rig attempting to place a pulser into the drilling hole. A metal cable on the hula band being used to guide the pulser into the hole caught his thumb and amputated it at the first joint.
An employee fell approximately 20 feet to the concrete ground below while installing angle iron at a steel erection site. The employee suffered cracked vertebrae and a cracked pelvis.

During a power outage, an employee was helping to clear a line of tree branches at an electrical substation using a pole pruner. A branch fell after it was cut, striking a live line and the employee.  The employee got shocked and was burned on his hands and torso.
While transitioning from a boat to the dock, an employee's foot slipped between the boat and the dock. He broke three toes on his right foot and was hospitalized for surgery on his big toe.
An employee attempted to retrieve a piece of ceramic material that broke off into the tape laminator machine he was using. His right index and middle fingertips were amputated by the machinery.

An employee was performing maintenance on a compressor unit. The compressor unit inside the building was shut off. The employee went to restart the compressor and a flash fire occurred. The employee suffered first and second degree burns to the hands, face, and arms, requiring hospitalization.
An employee was returning to base from a delivery when he was involved in a car accident. He was hospitalized.
An employee was working on an oil drilling rig. While attaching a check valve to a vertical pup joint, the employee's right index finger was pinched between the two parts, amputating the fingertip.
An employee had completed a run of five fasteners on an upsetter machine when their left hand got caught in the dies of the machine. The employee's left-hand pinky and ring fingers were amputated.

An employee had just spilled gasoline on himself while fueling a chainsaw. A coworker was smoking nearby and caused the injured employee's pants to catch on fire. The employee was burned and required hospitalization.
The injured employee contacted an energized electric line while directing roofing activities from a forklift-raised basket. He sustained electrical burns on his hand and was hospitalized.
While an employee was working underneath a truck to take out the drive shaft, a piece of metal fell into his eye. He was hospitalized for surgery.
An employee was cutting plastic laminate when the laminate moved and pulled his hand toward the saw. His index, middle, and ring fingers were partially amputated.

An employee was picking up trash on the roadway. She finished picking up the trash and got into the truck. A blanket in the truck blew out onto the road. She stopped the truck, pulled into the emergency lane, and got out to retrieve the blanket when she was struck by a passing pickup truck. She sustained extensive head trauma.

On August 31, 2015, at approximately 11:30 a.m., an employee was helping a concrete pumper during backup to position the concrete chute for pouring. As the truck was reversing with chute extended, it appeared as if the chute was going to strike against a switch gear unit. The employee attempted to push the chute to give it more clearance, but the chute was locked in position and wouldn't move. His finger got pinched between the chute and the switch gear unit, and his left pinky fingertip was amputated. He was hospitalized for surgery.

An employee suffered two broken ankles while hoisting a scale using an overhead crane. The scale had just been painted and was being lifted from a floor platform to be moved to an adjacent area for drying. The employee was raising the scale off the floor platform, taking up the slack of the rigging, when the scale slid off the platform and struck the employee's feet. Both ankles were broken from the impact.
While exiting a tugger, an employee did not clear the loader track and tripped over it, breaking the right ankle.
An employee was cutting a limb on the ground using a chainsaw. The tip of the saw popped out of the limb and struck the employee's left foot behind the big toe, causing a laceration.

An employee was changing hot oil from a deep fryer. The oil was placed in a pot on the floor, and the employee tripped on the pot handle while walking over the pot. The employee contacted the hot oil and sustained second degree burns.

Four employees were injured while attempting to set trusses on a barn. The trusses collapsed and the employees fell. Two of the employees were hospitalized. The first suffered a chipped shoulder bone and lacerations to his head. The second suffered compression fractures to three vertebrae.
While setting up the railings on a frac tank, an employee fell from the steps leading to the top of the tank to the ground, breaking his arm.
An employee was hospitalized with a broken hip after falling to the floor at work on August 31, 2015. The injured employee required surgery.
On August 31, 2015, an employee was cutting or clearing a tree for the company owner when he was struck by a falling limb, which gashed his head and injured his ribs. He was hospitalized.
An employee was walking on the roof and fell 8 feet to the ground. His head struck the ground and he sustained injuries requiring hospitalization.
While coming down a step ladder, an employee lost her footing on the bottom step and hit a door frame. Due to the impact, she injured the right side of her back.
An employee was attempting to pull a piece of plastic from a grinder plate. The employee's finger hit the rotating plate, resulting in a fingertip amputation.
An excavator backed over an employee's left foot, resulting in surgical amputation.
An employee needed to access a trailer to untangle a strap. While climbing a 4-foot ladder he lost his balance and fell to the floor, breaking a vertebra in his back.

An employee performing preventative maintenance was checking a roof vent. She removed the vent top and shut off the vent. Before the vent belt had stopped moving, her finger got pulled in between the pulley and belt. Her left pointer finger was amputated below the nail.
An employee was being trained on the fryer grill when a can of cooking spray that was left on top of a char-broiler exploded. The employee was burned and hospitalized overnight.
Two employees in a lift were installing a window when they fell approximately 11 feet to the ground. They were not tied off at the time.

An employee was wearing work gloves while operating a vertical milling machine to fabricate a tube. The employee attempted to adjust the tube in the machine with his left hand when his work glove got caught on a set screw. His left little fingertip was amputated; there was no bone loss.

On the ground level of the methyl acrylic acid (MAS) unit, an expansion joint became over-pressurized and exploded.  An employee in the area came in contact with MAS. One employee received chemical burns on his face, left arm, left mid-back, and left shoulder and was hospitalized.
An employee fell approximately 13 feet after stepping out onto a 2x4 while pulling wire. He sustained fractures to his left ankle and right leg.
An employee was adjusting the forks of a forklift when the fork settled into position, crushing his finger. It was later amputated.

At approximately 2:00 PM on 8/31/15, an employee was trying to retrieve the tip of a plunger that fell into a molten metal receiver. As he reached to retrieve the plunger, molten metal contacted and burned his left hand, requiring hospitalization.

An employee was transferring two metal bins half full of product to the mill area for production using a forklift truck. As he exited the truck to open the bin door, the bin fell on top of him, crushing the lower half of his body and breaking one leg.

While an employee was moving a small pile of hot material with a bobcat, a flash of steam entered the cab of the bobcat. The employee exited the cab and tripped into a pool of hot water, receiving first and second degree burns and requiring hospitalization.

An employee was filling concrete mix bags on the spout 
at the Old Castle/Anchor Concrete facility. The employee's finger got caught between the metal arms on the spout and the rubber bumpers, amputating the left index fingertip and nail.

An employee was observing empty shackles on the line to see if any required replacement. A high-pressure water hose was accidentally discharged into the throat of the injured employee by a coworker who was removing the hose from the wall hook. The injured employee suffered a laryngeal laceration and air in the neck.
While on his way back to the work office in the passenger seat of a vehicle, an employee suffered dehydration.

An employee was standing between pallets next to a wall. A pallet-jack operator, who was trying to drive around another worker, struck the pallets, which in turn struck the employee and fractured the right ankle.
An employee was bitten by a rattlesnake.

An employee was preparing to drill a hole in wax paper using a foot-operated paper drill machine. She placed a stack of paper in the machine using a block to hold the wax paper in place. When she pressed the foot pedal, the machine drilled the tip of her right index finger, causing an amputation-type injury.
An employee was riding on the back of a yard truck and got pinned between a trailer and the truck.

An employee was performing maintenance on a broach machine. The machine cycled while his hand was inside, amputating his three right-hand middle fingers. The machine guard was not in place at the time of the incident.
An employee operating a dump truck was emptying a load of dirt. The dump truck tipped over, and the employee suffered broken ribs, blood clotting, and lung issues.
An employee was installing water lines for PA American Water when he experienced dehydration from the heat, requiring hospitalization.

An employee was removing 1" piping from a reactor vessel for cleaning purposes. While removing the piping with a wrench tool, nitric acid leaked from the system and caused chemical burns to the employee's face and both arms.

An employee was doing iron fabrication work. While working on a circular saw, the blade "kicked" back the piece of flat strap iron, injuring the employee's left-hand middle finger. The injury resulted in an amputation (bone loss) along the fingertip.

On September 1, 2015, an employee parked his semi truck in the shop on the cement floor for servicing. He was going to lift the truck onto jack stands by first lifting it with the jack lift. While lifting the truck, the employee got down to the floor level to look beneath it. The handle of the jack lift fell, striking his left-hand little finger against the floor and resulting in a fingertip amputation.
An employee was struck by a car in a crosswalk while walking between buildings at the hospital. The employee sustained back and spine fractures.
An employee was tightening a clamp on the top of a mixing drum. The drum moved, and the employee fell more than 6 feet to the ground below, breaking both ankles and requiring hospitalization.
An employee was performing pipe maintenance work while exposed to high temperatures. He suffered heat exhaustion and was hospitalized.

An employee was responding to a call of the A/C unit inside the attic not operating. She fell approximately 8 feet to the floor below through an open hatch in the attic, breaking her ankle and sustaining a head injury.
An employee was climbing into a bulldozer when wind caused the door to shut on and amputate his thumb.

An employee was assembling a side belt driven conveyor. While checking the motor during the assembly, he noticed a clicking noise. He inspected what was causing the noise while the machine was running. His hand slipped while using a hand tool to adjust the chain that runs the motor, and his thumb went in between the chain and gear. He sustained a partial right thumb amputation.
Employee was walking near the loading dock at a Giant Eagle Store. He tripped over the dock lowering lever, fell, and broke his leg, requiring surgery.

An employee was operating a chop saw to cut pieces of aluminum. He was holding a piece of aluminum in place while making a cut when his right-hand thumb contacted the saw blade. He suffered a partial amputation of the thumb.

An employee was readjusting a sensor that controls tool pick up and tool changes. While he tried to check the position of the sensor, a coworker operated the Onsrud machine. The hood and airlines were not reattached. The back bush would not operate without the airline, so the injured employee attempted to hold up the back brush with his hand. The machine's platen dropped to pick up a tool; when it ascended, it caught the employee's thumb between the two platens, severely lacerating and fracturing it.
An employee was tearing off roof when his finger got pinched between a piece of plywood and a piece of machinery that was not in use. His left index finger was amputated.
An employee was repairing the coke oven door and pinched a fingertip behind the door latch resulting in the amputation of the fifth digit fingertip.
While attempting to clear a jam in a machine, an employee was struck by the compression cam, injuring her forearm. The machine was not shut down at the time.

A maintenance employee was in the laundry room lighting a water heater pilot. He had been using canned air to clear lint/dust from the area, then attempted to light the pilot, which caused a flash fire in his face. He suffered burns on his face and injuries to his eyes, requiring hospitalization.
An employee was hospitalized and treated for a infection from a blister that was caused by wearing safety boots.
An employee working on the forming line stepped back into the path of a forward-moving forklift and was struck. The employee's right foot was injured, requiring hospitalization.
While using a small lathe to polish a shaft, an employee's glove got caught. His arm was pulled under the part, breaking his forearm.
An employee fell while walking between his truck's catwalk and the trailer to get bungee cords to secure the trailer load. He broke three ribs, punctured a lung, and broke his collarbone.
An employee was loading plywood into a truck when his fingertip got smashed between the sheets of plywood. While pulling his finger out, the tip of the skin on his left ring finger tore off.
An employee dropped his cell phone after parking a golf cart. When he went to pick it up, a snake bit his right index finger.
On 09-01-15, at 01:45 AM, an employee went to retrieve a resident's call light. She tripped and fell over the resident's floor mat and was hospitalized.
An employee was walking when she fell and broke her hip.
An employee was attempting to clean a machine. While trying to clear chips away, his glove got caught and his left hand was pulled into the cutter, fracturing and lacerating his left hand and wrist.

An employee was climbing a ladder to reach the area where he was going to start anchoring the truss. He grabbed a nail gun that was hanging from the truss. It slipped from his hand and discharged a nail into his right leg, causing a puncture wound.
An employee was assembling testing equipment. The employee's left index finger got caught between a nut and an impact wrench and was amputated to the knuckle.
An employee was backing out of a flatbed truck. He lost his balance or slipped and hit his head on the ground, suffering a concussion.
An employee fell off an 8-foot step ladder while installing ductwork and sustained a compound fracture to his right ankle.
An employee strapping down cargo on a flatbed trailer slipped from the ratchet socket and twisted his ankle.
An employee was framing using a nail gun. A nail from the nail gun punctured his left leg above the knee, requiring hospitalization.
An employee operating a pallet jack went to drop off some pallets. He looked backwards and ran into a guard rail, fracturing his left leg.

An employee placed scaffold planks on scaffold tiebacks to create an elevated walkway above two sidewalk sheds. While traversing the walkway, the employee lost his balance and fell between the planks, bruising the inside of his left arm. He was hospitalized.

An employee attempted to replace the belt on an HVAC unit. The belt, which was still rotating, caught and amputated the employee's left index finger between the belt and pulley. The cover guard was not in place at the time of the incident.

An employee was stepping out of a material hoist when the hoist was struck by another piece of equipment. This caused the overhead protection on the hoist to collapse and strike the employee, who suffered a broken arm.
An employee was prepping his merchandise before loading it on a truck for delivery. He pulled his lower back muscle while shrink-wrapping a loveseat and was hospitalized.

An employee was standing at the entrance door of the valet parking office with his left hand resting on the hydraulic door cylinder while he was talking to co-workers. His left ring fingertip was pinched and amputated by the hydraulic cylinder arms when another employee opened the door to enter the office.
An employee passed out while repairing a tree trimmer. He was hospitalized for heat-related dehydration.

On 09/01/2015, at approximately 08:55 a.m., an employee was preparing to open the window section. She retrieved her money from the safe and placed it at the counter and then returned to the safe to secure her compartment and close the safe door. Her right thumb was smashed by the safe door as it closed. The bone was severed and the thumb was attached only by the skin. Her thumb was reattached at the hospital.
An employee was hanging string-line while constructing a wall. The employee's foot went between the forms and was lacerated by the wall ties, requiring surgery to repair the cut tendon.
An employee was manually moving a shelving unit in the pharmacy when she experienced numbness in her left arm.

An employee was operating a carton filler machine when the machine began to jam. While attempting to clear the jam, the employee's hand contacted the moving chain conveyor system. The employee's left-hand thumb fat pad, first index finger knuckle, and middle finger middle knuckle were amputated.injuring his head
While walking to the restroom, an employee slipped and fell to the ground, fracturing her hip.
While moving a pole with a bar, an employee experienced back pain.
An employee was washing out a tank with hot water that was about 130 to 140 degrees. The hot water scalded his back, resulting in third degree burns.
An employee was performing preliminary work before siding work when a guardrail gave way, causing the employee to fall from a third-story platform to the ground. The employee broke both legs.

An employee was repairing a commercial roof when he stepped off a small drop and lost his balance. He grabbed onto the hot mop cart to keep from falling and he was splashed with hot asphalt, sustaining burns to his head and back and requiring hospitalization.

An employee suffered a severe laceration to three fingers while cutting OSB boards on a table saw in the research and development shop. The table saw blade was not guarded at the time of the incident. The employee was hospitalized overnight.

An employee was handling a belt and pulley system machine, attempting to get the pulley to move, when his right-hand pinky finger got caught in the belt. His finger was dangling, and most likely suffered an amputation. The guard was not in place at the time of the incident.
An employee's right femur broke when a vehicle he was lowering off of a tow truck rolled into him and pinned him against a wall.
An employee was using a self-propelled lawn mower when he slipped and fell. His left hand went under the mower, resulting in middle and ring fingertip amputations.
An employee was standing on the back of a truck waiting to collect trash when he fell off, hitting his head on the pavement.
On September 2, 2015, an employee was refilling a hole in the ground using his foot when he stepped on a screw. The injury became infected.

An employee suffered an open fracture and amputation of the tissue of the right index finger when it got caught between the form station and vacuum seal while troubleshooting a form/fill/seal machine.

On September 2, 2015, an employee was mopping/cleaning a church floor when she slipped and fell on the wet surface, striking the back of her head on the floor. She sustained serious head injuries and required hospitalization.
An employee was examining electrical boxes to investigate a partial power loss within the facility. An arc flash occurred, and the employee suffered burns to the face, throat, and hands.

On September 2, 2015, at 10:30 a.m., an employee was in an elevated man basket approximately 20 feet above ground, stapling the copper ground wire to a utility pole, when he received an electrical shock through his right shoulder and left hand. He was hospitalized. PPE equipment was not used at the time of the incident.
On September 2, 2015, an employee was setting up garage door headers using a hand trowel when he began to experience cramping. He was hospitalized overnight due to heat exhaustion and dehydration.

An employee exited his dump truck and approached a trackhoe operator. The trackhoe had a piece of concrete barrier in its grasp about 6 inches off the ground. The concrete barrier rolled onto the employee's right foot and leg, resulting in broken leg/foot.

An employee was installing cornices on the side of the house using an approximately 8-foot multipurpose portable ladder when he fell on his back with his gear. The impact of the fall caused the employee to go into a coma.

On September 2, 2015, an employee was removing clay tile and installing a membrane on the roof of a building on the Capitol grounds. The employee began to experience cramping and was eventually hospitalized for possible dehydration.
An employee was working from a 6-foot step ladder when the ground gave way. The employee fell off of the ladder and hit a concrete window well, breaking four ribs on his right side.

On September 2, 2015, at 4:00 p.m., an employee had finished trimming some branches while suspended in a tree in a climbing saddle. He was descending when the knot that secured his lifeline to his safety harness clip came loose. He fell approximately 14 feet to the ground and suffered a compression fracture to his L-4 vertebrae in his spine, requiring hospitalization.
An employee was struck by a tractor trailer while it was backing up to another trailer to transfer product resulting in severe trauma to the abdomen requiring multiple surgeries.
An employee walked into a unit while walking and talking with a coworker; his right leg collapsed/fractured.
An employee standing on an extension ladder was replacing a flag on a property when the pole broke, causing him to fall on his back. He was hospitalized overnight.
An employee was working along the roof trusses doing fire proofing work approximately 9' high when he fell through the trusses. He was hospitalized overnight with minor bruises and scratches.

An employee was operating a steer loader, gathering parts to put together a feed bin. He pulled the steer loader up to the parts trailer.  There was a vehicle parked close to the trailer.  The employee got out of the steer loader, which was still running. His leg got jammed between the loader and the vehicle, resulting in a broken leg.

A maintenance employee was changing a belt on a fan in a paint booth when the other fans in the booth turned on. This caused the employee's fan to spin, and his finger got caught between the belt and pulley. His left ring finger got crushed and was later amputated. His right index finger was injured and required stitches.

A forklift operator was transporting a roll of material to the coating machine; their view was obstructed by the roll. As the forklift  approached the coating machine, the injured employee, who was standing at the machine controls, was struck in the lower right leg by the forklift and/or the material pallet. The employee sustained injuries to the lower right ankle and tibia bones.

On September 2, 2015, at approximately 3:15 p.m., a maintenance employee was attempting to adjust a moving conveyor that was off track (not centered) when he tripped on dry clay that had fallen from the conveyor onto the floor and fell into a slow moving conveyor, fracturing his right arm and requiring hospitalization.
An employee was descending a fixed ladder when he slipped and fell approximately 4 feet to the ground, injuring his back and left foot.

An employee was removing the belt from the pulley of an air handler when his fingers got caught between the pulley and belt. His right pinky fingertip was amputated. LO/TO was in place when this incident happened.
An employee lost two joints on their right middle finger while attempting to remove scraps from in and around a moving saw blade.
An employee was cutting lumber with a Skill saw when he hit a knot in the wood, which caused him to lose control of the saw. As a result, the tip of his left thumb was amputated.
After operating a hydraulic excavator, an employee began to experience heart-attack-like symptoms. The employee was hospitalized overnight for dehydration possibly due to heat.
An employee was using a chainsaw to clear vegetation from a customer's powerlines. He was hospitalized for severe dehydration and high levels of enzymes in the kidneys due to heat exposure.
An employee was driving a four-wheeled all terrain vehicle on a paved road. The employee was involved in an accident and received a brain injury.
An employee was installing water irrigation piping and pivots. A pipe broke and hit the employee on the arm, breaking it and resulting in hospitalization and surgery.
An employee was mowing grass on a hillside when the lawn mower tipped over and rolled over him. He sustained a back laceration and internal bleeding.
An employee was looking at excess equipment in an area with limited visibility. He fell approximately 4 feet from the floor area to the asphalt rail-bed area and broke his a rib.

An employee was preparing to run a new cable line from a utility pole to a house. The employee leaned a 28-foot ladder against the cable strand and was climbing or working when the staple fastener that was holding a strand support came out of the pole. The strand then fell 4 feet and the employee fell from the ladder, sustaining a serious head injury and other broken bones.
An employee was operating a forklift to gather merchandise. His right index finger got caught and amputated between the side of the forklift and the horizontal bracket.
While prepping a pipeline prior to painting, an employee was bitten on the left middle finger by a rattlesnake. He was hospitalized for treatment.

An employee was handling hides to get them in the deflesher when the "gripper" jaws opened and shut on the employee's left pinky. The employee sustained a soft tissue amputation of the left pinky finger.

An employee was practicing riding on a pallet jack during training when he pressed the rabbit button instead of the horn, causing the pallet jack to move faster. The employee quickly dismounted the pallet jack and landed on the concrete floor, breaking his left ankle.
An employee was delivering mail in a residential area when a dog chased after him as he crossed the street. He fell down a 5.5-foot retention wall embankment, breaking his pelvis and vertebrae.

An employee was operating a forklift to move equipment, which became unstable and started tipping. The employee dismounted the forklift to steady the equipment, which struck the employee, resulting in a broken tibia and contusions to other parts of the body.
An employee became ill while operating the treatment plant at the Susquehanna River intake and was hospitalized.
An employee was using a band saw to cut boneless pit hams in half to run them through a slicer. The band saw motor ran in reverse, and the employee's middle and ring fingertips were amputated.

An employee was helping to install a wiring system into a residential property. The employee leaned a ladder against the side of the property's gutter system. A 3"x6' gutter cover dislodged and struck the employee in the arm, resulting in a 3-inch laceration to the bone. The employee was hospitalized with muscle and tendon damage.
On or about September 2, 2015, at 5:45 a.m., a General Bakery employee's left thumb was amputated after it was caught between a rake tool and the side of the mixing tank.
An employee was working on the drive sprocket of a fryer when the drive chain grabbed his glove and pulled his finger into the sprocket. His finger was partially amputated.

An employee was operating a brake press. She reached for a piece of metal and stepped on the press pedal. The press cycled and partially amputated her right middle and ring fingers, requiring surgery.
Two employees engaged in a fight. One employee bit the injured employee's ear off, resulting in an amputation.
On 9-2-15, an employee was making a bed. When she leaned over the bed, she felt a pain in her back. She was hospitalized with a back injury.
An employee fell approximately 10-12 feet while descending the ladder from the top of the railcar.
An employee was loading bags of cement/asphalt onto a cart at Lowe's when a wheel on the cart broke. The cart collapsed onto the employee's foot, amputating a toe.

A forklift operator was driving the lift back to the dock area when he struck the injured employee. The front side of the forklift hit the employee, then the right front tire ran over his foot.  He was hospitalized, where his foot up to his calf (left leg) was amputated.
An employee was hospitalized with left ankle and knee injuries when he fell through the skylight on the roof while trimming trees from around the building.

An employee was loading parts into a machine when one twisted out of place. The employee tried to adjust the part with their right index finger, which got caught in the machine and was amputated just above the fingernail.
An employee delivering packages felt dizzy and later experienced cramping in the legs. She was hospitalized for dehydration.
An employee was nailing a form together to pour concrete in when he slipped and injured his back.

An employee was training on the Columbia River, 0.5 miles west of Astoria, deploying oil boom on the aft deck when the boom line got stuck. The employee tried to free the line, but it was under tension.  The line came free, snapped straight, and struck his leg, fracturing his ankle and knee.
An employee was working to set a tool up to start torqueing when his pinky finger got caught between the hydraulic torque wrench and a part. He dislocated his pinky finger.

An employee was dismantling a canopy with a wrench while standing on the cross braces. The employee lost their footing and fell approximately 14 feet to the concrete pavement, sustaining a head injury and requiring hospitalization.
An employee was walking in a carpeted area.  She tripped where the carpet meets that tile at the rubber threshold, hitting her head and injuring her left elbow and both knees.
An employee was bleeding pressure from a 4" line.  In the process, a 2" riser pipe ruptured, and the employee was struck in the right leg by flying debris. The employee's foot was amputated.

An employee was conducting work on the 60-feet-high platform of an oil derrick, operating rigging to move piping into position. The employee became sick, vomited, experienced cramps, and was eventually hospitalized for heat-related health issues.
An employee had just finished repairing the chip mill saw. While walking on the metal decking, he tripped on saw dust, hit the decking, and fractured his left femur bone.

An employee was putting duct tape on a press machine. The operator jogged the machine, and the employee's finger got caught in the perforation wheel. The employee's left middle fingertip was amputated.
On or about September 3, 2015, an employee amputated or partially amputated three right-hand fingers when they got caught in a sprocket while replacing a chain on the sprocket drive.
An employee's H2S monitor went off while he was delivering salt water on location. He eventually became ill and was hospitalized with respiratory problems.
On September 3, 2015, an employee sustained a head injury. While he was looking at a piece of wood, he tripped and hit his head, requiring overnight hospitalization.

An employee was outside the west dock changing spotlights, using a 6-foot step ladder. The ladder shifted and fell over with the employee on it. The employee sustained a separated right shoulder, broken toe, broken right femur, and facial lacerations.
An employee was conducting an intervention with a client (patient). The client pushed her, causing her to fall and dislocate/fracture her right wrist.
An employee was filling propane cylinders for forklifts when a flash fire occurred. The employee sustained first and second degree burns on both sides of their torso and arms.

An employee was standing in a sewer ditch while guiding a 10-foot steel pipe into position when the device holding the pipe slipped due to the plastic cover. The pipe struck the employee on his right tibia, causing a fracture.
An employee's arm was injured when it was caught between a chair and desk while he was working at his desk.

An employee activated a pneumatic holding mechanism by foot pedal while placing a plastic door on a machine. The clamp pinched the employee's right middle finger between the clamp and the plastic door. When the employee pulled their finger out, the right middle finger nail and skin were removed.

An employee was working on a front-end loader, taking the lift cylinder from the hood. The employee had the hood at a 90-degree angle. The hood moved and struck the employee on the leg, fracturing both bones in the lower left leg.
While attempting to free a jammed leather piece from a mechanical press, an employee's left arm was crushed when the press activated. His arm was surgically amputated at the hospital.

On September 3, 2015, at approximately 9:30-10 a.m., an employee was mowing with a zero turn mower. The employee dismounted the mower as it approached a chain link fence. The mower rolled and struck the employee, breaking his hip and requiring hospitalization.

An employee was operating a stand-up forklift and preparing to put a pallet away.  He backed up the lift and the heel of his left foot made contact with the pallet rack behind him, causing crushing injuries to his toes.
An employee worked on his knees on the subfloor of the IT room for two days. He developed knee pain, knee swelling, and fever.
An employee was performing grounds keeping work when his eyeglasses fell to the ground. As he searched for them, a coral snake bit his left-hand middle finger.
An employee loaded some roof trusses onto a flatbed truck. He started to band the load when one of the roof jacks fell and hit his head, resulting in internal bleeding and hospitalization.

An employee was threading a machine with film onto a take-up roll. After changing over from job mode to run mode, the injured employee noted a problem with the film take-up roll and entered the area to address the issue. While doing so, his upper arm got caught in the ingoing spool. His upper arm broke and required surgery.
An employee using a power shear amputated a digit on his left index finger when his finger got caught between the shear blades.

An employee was unloading a mold from Press 12 to a cart for transport. The cart got stuck on a fatigue mat and tipped over. The handle of the cart struck the interior of the employee's left foot, fracturing it.

An employee was forming a footing for a water treatment plant. He was working inside a 4-feet-tall trench form and fell while crossing back over to the outside of the trench, breaking his right tibia and fibula.

An employee was preparing rice for the Brandeis University catering service. When the rice was finished cooking, the employee pulled the hotel pan out of the cooker. The residual water left over from the cooking process splashed out of the pan and onto the employee's lower right arm, causing second degree burns.
An employee was using a cutoff saw to cut a 10-inch concrete pipe when the saw kicked back, cutting the employee's collarbone.
An employee was on an 8-foot A-ladder, looking over the company van, when he fell 3.5 feet to the ground. He dislocated his right knee and broke his left elbow, requiring surgery.

On September 3, 2015, at 3:30 p.m., an employee's left pinky finger got caught in the lift chain of a forklift. The bottom third of his pinky finger was amputated, requiring overnight hospitalization.

city: M C B H KANEOHE BAY
final_narrative: An employee working in the pool area was hospitalized for infection.
An employee was cutting a fallen tree limb when it became unstable, rolled, and knocked him off of a deck to the ground roughly 11 feet below. The employee sustained broken ribs.
An employee was walking on a working surface when plywood fell over and struck his leg, breaking it.
An employee fell while hanging baskets and struck their head, sustaining a concussion.

An employee was heating a bag of soup. As she pulled the bag of soup from the kettle containing hot water, the bag of soup broke, causing first and second degree burns on her torso and left arm.  She was hospitalized.
On or about 9/3/15, a temp worker injured her finger while operating a printing machine in the Cardboard Box Department.  Part of her finger had to be amputated.

An employee was using a table saw to cut wood and attempted to clear a jam. When the employee cleared the jam, the saw activated and amputated his middle finger, severed his pointer finger, and mutilated his thumb.
An employee was moving a resident's care bed. Her left pinky finger got caught in a pinch point between a closet door and the bed, crushing her fingertip. The fingertip was surgically amputated.
An employee was driving a concrete buggy to move concrete when the buggy tipped, causing him to dismount the buggy. He landed on his feet on the concrete surface and fractured his hip.

An employee was slicing cucumbers on the deli slicer. While attempting to retrieve a piece of cucumber, the employee's right hand made contact with the blade, resulting in a right fingertip and fingernail amputation.

An employee was removing railing to convert the Pepsi Center floor from a basketball arena to a concert arena. The employee fell over the railing onto the concrete floor, dislocating his hip and suffering a concussion.
On 9/4/15, an employee was injured when she tripped over another employee's foot and fell. She broke her hip and required surgery.

An employee was installing a light fixture from a scissor lift when the railing broke. The employee fell about 10 feet, injuring their hip and breaking three foot bones. The employee required hip surgery.

An employee was working on a third floor balcony, applying flashing to metal. The employee stepped through the floor joists, landed on the second floor balcony, and then fell to the first floor. The employee sustained broken ribs, a broken ankle, and a punctured lung and was hospitalized.

Employees were setting a canopy in place using a lull.  The injured employee used a fiberglass extension ladder to climb to the top of the 9'-high canopy to remove a sling. He fell from the ladder and fractured both wrists and two ribs.
An employee was cleaning the shredder with an air wand when the air wand swung back and struck the employee. The employee sustained a laceration from the throat to the ear and was hospitalized.

An employee was moving furniture using a box truck with a hydraulic lift gate on the back. As he and a coworker raised the lift gate, he got off the lift and grabbed the side of the rail. The coworker began to operate the lift again, which caught and amputated the employee's thumb.
An employee sustained a broken ankle while stepping off of a four-rung ladder.
An employee was pouring concrete with a hose. Air got into the line and the hose struck him in the head and neck.

An employee was transferring fuel to the gas station when a fire occurred. The employee sustained burns to 46 percent of his body, 3 percent of which were third degree burns to both arms and his back.

An employee was coming down from an attic after delivering blown insulation materials using a 12-foot extension ladder. The employee fell approximately 9'10" from the ladder to the concrete floor and fractured his back. The ladder did not have anti-slip feet.

An employee was holding a slab of quartz. He tried to separate two slabs when the momentum and weight fell back on him. He then tried to push them back and step out of the way of the falling quartz, but he fell and hit his head. He broke his leg and required head stitches.
An employee was going to hand a piece of material to a coworker. At that time, a coil pusher was activated. The employee's left foot was then crushed between the pusher arm and coil stock.

An employee fell 10 feet from a mezzanine during welding operations, injuring their left shoulder tendon, cracking the L4 vertebra, and lacerating the left arm. A guardrail was not in place at the time of the incident.
An employee was unloading railcars. While climbing down a railcar ladder, the employee missed a step and fell, fracturing both heels.

An employee was disassembling a one-tier tubular scaffold. The employee removed the cross bracing first. When a coworker removed the planks, the scaffold members came down and struck the employee, causing back and pelvis bruises.

On or about September 4, 2015, at 12:09 p.m., an employee was riding on the right rear step of a garbage truck during a right-hand turn. He was knocked off of the step when his shoulder contacted an illegally parked semi-tractor trailer, and he fell onto the street, hitting his head and knocking him unconscious.  He was hospitalized for a concussion and subdural hematoma.
On or about September 4, 2015, an employee working in the small sort area injured the skin on her right middle finger when her hand contacted the conveyor belt.
While working on a metal part on a brake press, the employee amputated the tip of his left index finger.
An employee injured her back while lifting packaging film.

An employee was moving an oil field casing/pipe-related materials in and out of a pipe rack with a forklift. The pipes rolled down the rack and pinched/lacerated the employee's fingertip, which had to be amputated.

On September 5, 2015, an employee was operating a wind-up machine when the light curtain failed. The overhead press roll activated and came down on the employee's head. The employee sustained a severe head contusion and laceration.
An employee broke a knee while climbing down a ladder. The employee was hospitalized and required surgery.

On or about September 5, 2015, an employee in the garden department was assisting a customer when he began to feel unwell and passed out.  The employee fell to the floor, striking his head.  He was hospitalized overnight for heat exhaustion and dehydration.

An employee was cleaning the deck and noticed a 10' piece of angle iron in the way.  The employee attempted to move the angle iron when the left side of it became wedged between concrete and a metal support.  The employee was standing next to an I-beam support structure.  As the employee tried to move the angle iron back and forth, he slammed his right hand between the angle iron and the I-beam, pinching his right pinky finger and amputating the fingertip.

While cleaning the blade area on a hock cutter the "double trigger" was inadvertently activated resulting in the amputation of the left index finger to the first knuckle and a partial amputation of the tip of the middle finger.

An employee was threading yarn through the winder with his right hand on the aspirator. The traverse (yarn holder) grabbed his left pinky finger and lacerated it. His left ring finger was also lacerated. The pinky finger had to be surgically amputated to the first knuckle.
An employee was helping coworkers move a steel beam when the beam fell on the employee's left foot. The employee's left-foot phalanges were crushed and required surgery.
An employee went into a facility and got out of his truck to check into the guard shack. When he went back to get into his truck, he missed a step and fell to the ground, breaking his left arm.
An employee cooking in the kitchen opened a pot that was on the stove. The liquid spilled on the employee, burning their wrist and feet.
Employee was performing underwater manufacturing of lead styphnate when initiation occurred, causing second degree burns and contusions to the employee's face.
An employee slipped and fell while walking into a patient's room and was hospitalized with a broken hip.

An employee was driving through a construction zone after unloading production water at a disposal well when his vehicle veered off the road and crashed south of Killdeer, North Dakota, on Highway 22. He suffered back injuries.
An employee was cleaning the entrance of the car wash station. While walking in the back where the drainage goes, he stepped in an opening and injured his knee.

A firefighter was cutting line with the crew around spot fires in very steep terrain. A burning log rolled on top of the firefighter pinning him to the burning ground. The firefighter could not remove the log and neither could a crew member who tried to assist.  The firefighter suffered second degree burns to 23 percent of his back and third degree burns to seven percent of his right shoulder, chest, stomach and back of legs.
An employee injured his knee when he tripped on a rubber safety mat.

On September 7, 2015, at about 04:00 PM, an employee fell from a 4- to 5-foot scaffold while cutting an aluminum structure beam with a chain saw. The saw kicked back, causing the employee to lose his balance and fall to the concrete floor. He sustained a head laceration and was hospitalized.

An employee was cleaning an inclined conveyor that was approximately 9 to 10 feet off the ground.   The employee used a 10-foot A-frame fiberglass step ladder to access the working area. The employee's left hand got caught in the conveyor, resulting in a left wrist fracture. LO/TO was not performed at the time of the incident.
An employee was hospitalized with lower back pain after lifting patients at the hospital.

On 9/7/15, an employee was cleaning out top flash and trimmings that had fallen on the floor beneath an auto-trimmer. His finger entered the stroke path of the lift cylinder, and his right middle fingertip was amputated.

An employee was performing maintenance underneath a truck when the jack holding the truck into position slid/slipped, causing the vehicle to make contact with the employees right leg. The employee was hospitalized with a broken right leg.

Employees were starting the granulator when ammonia bypassed the control valve and bled into the granulator. Fumes were released while the employees were nearby, causing chemical burns, respiratory illness, and unconsciousness. Two employees were hospitalized.
An employee's right hand was injured while attempting to break a jam (conveyor bottle neck) on a conveyor.
An employee stumbled and broke his leg while pulling a load of water from a production tank.
An employee was blowing off a roof during a roof inspection. The employee fell 25 feet through a skylight to the floor below, sustaining a hip dislocation and possible broken bones.
An employee standing on the back of a trailer during an offload lost their footing. The employee fell to the ground and rolled their right ankle. The employee was hospitalized with a broken ankle.

An employee was unloading product from a stand-up forklift when the forklift began to slip on a wet floor. He attempted to press an emergency stop bar near the foot pedals, but his foot slipped and got caught between the forklift and a pole. His foot was lacerated and required surgery.

An employee was removing a sleeve that goes around a bar weighing approximately 50 to 100 pounds. The sleeve was secured with four bolts; three were partially removed and one was removed completely. As he turned the sleeve, his left ring finger got caught between the sleeve and bar, causing a partial amputation.
While making a delivery at a residential site, an employee lost consciousness and collapsed due to dehydration, requiring hospitalization.

While moving a large, heavy-duty stand-up fan, an employee's right thumb was severely lacerated to and/or through the bone by the fan blade. The employee was hospitalized. The fan was running at the time of the incident.
An employee was punching holes in a quarter-inch angle iron when the die broke and shattered. A chip of the die impaled the employee's chest.
An employee fell through a skylight while walking/working on the roof, sustaining multiple arm and leg injuries.
After installing a new roof at the Kendall Square community complex, an employee on his way back to the shop started experiencing cramps in the legs and stomach due to dehydration.

An employee was loading bar stock into the lathe when the bar stock became jammed. While he attempted to clear the jam, the energized clamp came down and pinched his finger, resulting in a right ring fingertip amputation (no bone).
An employee was removing sprinkler heads while working on top of a walk-in cooler. The employee fell and sustained a head injury that required staples and a possible broken shoulder.
An employee fell through a skylight approximately 15 feet to the ground, sustaining two fractured vertebrae in his lower back, lacerations, and bruises.

An employee was helping to install an elevator. He was lifting a counter weight frame while using a hoist. The rope being used got tangled in the cylinder. While attempting to straighten it, his hand got caught. He tried to withdraw his hand, and three fingertips were amputated.
An employee climbed a 6-foot ladder to trim a tree branch. The branch fell and knocked him to the ground. He broke his leg and fractured his skull.

An employee was pushing a deep fryer back into place after cleaning behind it. One of the fryer wheels became caught when a loose drain cover on the floor shifted. The fryer and employee fell, and the hot cooking oil in the fryer spilled onto the floor and onto the employee. He received 3rd degree burns on his right hand and on both legs from the knees down.
An employee was greasing a 2-inch valve with a high-pressure grease gun when the hose erupted in the employee's right palm, lacerating the palm of the right hand.
An employee amputated his thumb, index, and middle fingers while operating a foot-controlled chop saw to cut stock.

An employee was climbing a ladder to attach a metal jacket around a railroad car when the securement chain on the ladder came loose. The ladder became unstable and slid, causing the employee to fall and dislocate the left ankle. The employee required surgery.
An employee fell from a ladder, injuring a hip and fracturing an elbow bone and ribs.
On September 8, 2015, at 8:56 AM, an employee suffered a partial amputation of the right middle fingertip while wiping dust near the rotating shaft of a laminator machine.

An employee was walking while carrying a tub of mail. The employee's foot got caught on all-purpose container webbing, and the employee fell to the concrete floor. The employee was hospitalized for a broken rib on the left side and a collapsed left lung.
An employee was using a sledge hammer to drive stakes or conduct demolition activities when he overheated and fainted.
An employee sustained second and third degree burns while attempting to clean a flat-top grill with combustible liquid.
An employee was installing gutters from a ladder when he lost his balance and fell approximately 7 feet to the ground below. He broke his wrist and lower back.

An employee had just finished a delivery at a residential house and was descending the stairs from the property. While stepping downward off the stairs, the employee dislocated and broke their right ankle.
An employee fell to the floor while walking down a hallway, fracturing their right knee, wrist, and shoulder.

A maintenance employee was working on a snorkel lift that was up in the air. He reached down to retrieve something and steadied himself by placing his other hand on the sprocket. The sprocket moved and amputated his right thumb tip, including the nail. The lift guard was not in place at the time of the incident.

On September 8, 2015, at 10 a.m., an employee was walking down the roof to get a piece of plywood to lay down. His fall protection yo-yo locked and caused him to lose his balance. He fell off the edge to the ground below in the building, injuring his head and requiring hospitalization.

An employee hooked up a hose to unload sulfuric acid. After he hooked up the appropriate hose, he walked around the truck to make sure everything was in its proper place. He then came back and touched the hose to ensure that sulfuric acid was being transferred. When he touched the hose, it came off, and the sulfuric acid splashed all over him and contacted his neck. He sustained third degree burns to his neck and shoulder and second degree burns to his arm. He was wearing PPE at the time.
An employee was performing maintenance duties when a range bull got out of its pasture. The bull head butted her and broke her pelvis.

An employee was loading a trailer using a powered industrial truck. When the employee exited the truck, it rolled forward and pinned the employee between the truck and the trailer. The employees ribs and vertebrae were fractured.
An employee slipped and fell while walking to the water fountain, hitting her head on the floor. She injured the left side of her head and her upper neck.

An employee felling a tree looked up at the tree being cut. A branch from the falling tree caught his wire safety glasses, knocking them off and allowing a branch to cut his eye. His iris/cornea was detached.

On September 7, 2015, an employee's left ankle was swollen after working in the acetic acid unit to clear/de-inventory the purification section. He was eventually hospitalized for ankle blisters and chemical burns.

An employee was changing a swab on a mud pump using a wrench to stroke the pump. The pipe wrench slipped and he fell backwards off the skid to the ground. His back and head struck the ground and he injured his chest. He sustained a head laceration, upper right bicep cut, chest contusion, and concussion.

During moving activities, three employees unsecured and then lost control of the end piece of a gantry crane. The piece rolled out from under them and struck the injured employee's foot, amputating his right big toe and requiring hospitalization.

An employee was driving a forklift when the load contacted the overhead lighting, dislodging it from the overhead trusses. The employee then attempted to secure the lighting fixture to prevent it from falling. He used a scissor lift to access the light and was in the process of securing it when he touched the fixture, receiving an electric shock and burns to the left ring finger, as well as left arm numbness.
An employee was cutting a watermelon with a knife when the watermelon rolled and caused the knife to slip. The employee's right middle finger was amputated.
An employee removing metal flashing from a parapet wall was shocked when the metal flashing contacted a 7200-volt overhead power line, burning the employee's left wrist and right arm/hand.

An employee was operating a stand-up forklift near rack storage units. His hand got caught between the rear of the forklift and the stored material as he was reversing the forklift. He sustained a crushing injury and lacerations to his left hand.
While setting a gearbox in the motor for a tank mixer, an employee's hand got caught between the gearbox and mounting plate. The employee's left hand was crushed.

An employee was working on the bar straightening machine when the straightener jammed and was shut down. The bar went back and forth, then came back and crushed the employee's finger, resulting in amputation.
An employee fell off of a large moving truck while moving furniture, sustaining a head laceration and dislocated shoulder.

An employee was checking on a heater-type coil in a refrigerator/freezer unit in the basement of the facility. The employee was working on the unit with two alligator clips in each hand while possibly standing in water; the plug was 110 voltage. The employee sustained a possible electrical shock.
An employee was on a ladder when it folded and fell to the ground. The employee suffered lacerations and a concussion.

An employee was using a 4-inch grinder to cut a piece of rebar when it kicked back and he cut his left hand on the inner part of the left thumb and his wrist on the grinder. He received a cut approximately 1/4-inch long and was hospitalized for surgery. Gloves were worn at the time of the incident.
An employee attempted to correct a misaligned end shield on a press he was using for trimming. The press cycled, cutting his left hand and fracturing three fingers.

An employee was using a torch to heat up a stuck stud on the tank. The torch ignited methanol gas that was put in the tank the day before.  The employee was thrown back 6 to 7 feet and received second and third degree burns to the abdomen.

An employee was replacing a hydraulic lift cylinder on a forklift. As he unbolted the oil line, the second stage of the forklift began to drop, lacerating and crushing his finger between the frame and the second stage. He was hospitalized for surgery.
An employee suffered from heat exhaustion and passed out while operating the concrete truck controls.

An employee was working with a tire/wheel change-out machine for a large tractor tire. The tire flipped out of the machine on top of the employee, amputating his left-hand pinky finger and injuring his hand.
While feeding wood into the notching machine, an employee's left pinky fingertip was amputated on the machine's infeed.
An employee preparing to move backhoe forks fractured his right femur when part of the forks fell on his leg. He also lacerated his right ring finger.

An employee was fighting a fire in a remote area. The employee had an extra drip torch, which had leaked fuel. The residual fuel caught on fire, and the employee sustained second degree burns on the back of the arm, above the left elbow in the triceps area, as well as burns around both legs/sock areas.
An employee was crating a window with a nail gun. As he switched the nail gun from one hand to the other, the gun shot a nail into his right leg.

An employee was working outdoors installing a CO2 line at a restaurant. The employee exhibited heat stress-related symptoms, including shortness of breath and cramping, and was hospitalized overnight.
An employee preparing meals at a residential home slipped and fell on the floor, fracturing a hip.

An employee attempted to adjust the air pressure on the UBE machine while working on the packaging line. The employee's finger got caught in a chain and sprocket that was attached to the machine, amputating the right index fingertip.
An employee fell into an 8-foot deep trench while trying to cross it, injuring his lower back and spine.
An employee was patrolling the building/perimeter when the employee tripped and fell to the ground, breaking the right hip.
An employee was cutting board for an exhibit on a table saw when the board kicked back and struck the employee's abdomen.
On or about September 9, 2015, an employee's finger was amputated while slicing meat with a meat band saw.

An employee was sweeping next to the wash pad rail system around 7:40 a.m. An aerial lift (enclosed with tarp) used for abrasive blasting stopped to drive a short distance to a new area. The employee grabbed the tarp to move it out of the way, and the employee's foot got caught and was struck, requiring hospitalization.

An employee was operating a metal pipe bender in the bender work area. The employee was attempting to adjust the bender when a coworker cycled the machine. The employee's left-hand pinky and ring fingers were crushed, and the distal phalanx of the left-hand middle and ring fingers were surgically removed.
While replacing a gasket in a vibration fixture, a maintenance employee's finger got caught in a pinch point when the fixture dropped 1.5 inches. His index finger was amputated.
An employee fractured his hand while connecting a trailer when his hand got caught in the trailer's hydraulic cylinder.

An employee was cleaning the rubbers on the entry end of the slitter head when his arm was pulled into the machine. He broke his left-hand pinky and ring fingers and required a skin graft between his elbow and wrist.
An employee was using an alligator shear to cut a nickel alloy plate when his hand and thumb contacted the shear's nip point. The bone behind his knuckle was crushed/fractured.

An employee was moving a new transformer into location. The employee leaned against the old transformer, which was still energized, causing metal to push into the energized bus bar. An arc flash occurred, and the employee sustained burns.

An employee was machining a packing tube when a bushing on the bar came loose. The employee attempted to push the bushing back in place and his left hand got caught in the rotating bar, amputating his left index finger and fracturing the adjacent fingers. The employee was wearing gloves at the time of the incident.

An employee was working on a crane motor. As the motor started, it backfired through the exhaust where the employee was standing. He jumped from the crane chassis to the floor (approximately 4 feet) and fractured his left knee. He was hospitalized.
An employee fell and broke her hip while descending from a ladder.
On September 9, 2015, at 8:50 a.m., an employee's bare hand made contact with an energized heating coil in a rooftop unit, resulting in second and third degree hand burns.
An employee was adding sealant to an air handler unit when the sealant container ruptured, injuring the employee's hands. He was hospitalized.
An employee was working from a sidewalk shed when he fell and broke his wrist.
On 9/9/2015, an employee suffered a right ring fingertip amputation and fractured rib when a storage rack containing tires fell on top of him after being struck by his forklift.

An employee was on the third step of a ladder tightening a plug on a boiler unit. He slipped and fell approximately 3 feet to the floor, lacerating his head, breaking a bone in his back, dislocating his right big toe, and bruising his elbow. He was hospitalized.
An employee was cutting flooring material using a table saw. His hand slipped, and his right index finger and thumb were cut. The index finger and thumb tip were amputated at the hospital.

At 10:30 a.m. on the production floor, an employee attempted to unjam one of the pads on the PAD machine. The blade on the machine amputated her left-hand index finger from the bed of the fingernail to the tip. She was hospitalized. The machine was still running at the time of the incident.

An employee was walking back to the production area after leaving the break area when his foot or the edge of his pants got caught onto a pallet causing the employee to trip and fall to the concrete floor.  The employee broke a hip as a result of the fall.
An employee was operating a yard tractor when he tripped and was run over by the tractor. He sustained a chest and abdominal injury.
An employee suffered from heat exhaustion while cutting 2x4's on a bridge.
An employee using the restroom slipped and tore her ACL.

On September 10, 2015, an employee was attempting to close a door to a patient's room while the patient was trying to pull it open. The door slammed shut and the employee's right index finger was caught between the door and the door jam, crushing his fingertip. The fingertip was later surgically amputated.
An employee was carrying plywood and suffered from heat exhaustion.
An employee was removing the cutter head of an auger when his left arm got caught between the auger and the casing. His left arm was amputated.
An employee was moving a post-con cart when her foot got caught in the cart webbing. She fell onto the ground and hurt/broke her left hip.
An employee fell approximately 8 feet and hit his head on the ground while descending an extension ladder. He fractured the orbital bone in his head.
While adjusting the jack foot pad for an equipment trailer, an employee's left index fingertip was amputated as he was aligning cotter pin holes.

An employee was performing maintenance on the motor to a raw incline auger when their fingers were caught between the belt and pulley on the motor. LO/TO was not performed. The employee suffered an open left pinky finger fracture.
An employee was adjusting an elbow machine when their left-hand fingers got caught in the machine's clamp, dislocating and fracturing the second and third fingers.

An employee and a coworker were at servicing a truck. The employee was under the truck close to the fuel tanks when the coworker started the truck. The truck moved forward and the rear tandem caught the employee and drug him an unknown distance.

An employee was using a grinder to remove tack welds from a 12" by 4.5" steel plate. While grinding, the steel plate broke free and struck the employee's left eye. The employee sustained a left cheek and left eyebrow laceration, as well as a fractured left orbital eye socket.

An employee was checking the gauging on an upper die shoe. The upper die shoe slipped/fell off the pins, and the employee turned and hit the cutting edge of the die. The employee sustained a left pointer finger soft tissue amputation.

An employee was helping to set dies when his left hand got struck by the die as it was being lowered into the parallel. His left-hand middle finger was injured and had to be amputated to the second knuckle.
An employee cutting manufactured parts with a vertical band saw lacerated their left index finger, requiring surgery.
An employee was attempting to clear a jam on a machine when the blade came down and cut her left middle finger.
An employee was attempting to repair a cable from a ladder. As he descended, the ladder moved and he fell. He got caught between the steps and broke his right leg.

An employee was cutting a doorway frame using a saw when the frame fell onto the employee and struck the back of his hand. The nails or other protrusions punctured the skin on his right hand. He was hospitalized.
An employee was placing sheeting over the stairway to a basement when he lost consciousness and fell 8 feet over the exposed edge to the lower level. He injured his head and was hospitalized.

An employee was ensuring that material was not in a bind while being processed on a conveyor. The employee's arm got pinched between the conveyor roller and the underside of the conveyor belt, sustaining skin abrasions.
An employee was attempting to remove the lid from a ladle that contained molten metal. The molten metal splashed onto the employee, burning his right arm, right hand, and back.
An employee was attaching clamps to a hide at the side puller station on the kill side of the plant when his left thumb got caught in the clamp. He sustained a left thumb avulsion.
An employee tripped over a linen cord, breaking both wrists and fracturing her knee. She was hospitalized for surgery.
An employee tripped over a floor mat and fell to the ground in the administrative hallway. The employee was hospitalized for a tear in the right knee ligament.
Half of an employee's right pinky finger was amputated by a lumber planner he was operating.
An employee fell off the steps while he was working with a shear press machine on the platform. He fractured his right hip.

An employee was in the cleanup/pump room delivering tools and helping to change belts on a pump. While helping to remove an old guard from a machine to put on a new one, he amputated his right-hand middle and ring fingertips.

On Sunday, September 6, 2015, a forestry technician (hot shot) had physical training.  After the training, the hot shot felt more tired than usual for a few days.  On September 9, 2015, the hot shot had his left knee examined for a previous injury.  During the exam, the physician noticed swelling in the arms and recommended blood work. The blood work indicated a muscle injury due to physical training in hot conditions and the hot shot was admitted to the hospital for treatment in the morning on September 10, 2015.
An employee was breaking down mail when her foot got tangled in plastic straps, causing her to fall and fracture her right shoulder and right knee.

On September 10, 2015, at 1:40 PM, an employee's right ring finger was partially amputated by a wire straightening machine. He was checking the gears when one of the tracks fell and cut off his fingertip.
An employee was working on the front corner of the house tearing off drip edge. He had a seizure and fell seven feet off the roof resulting in possible broken ribs. Fall protection was not worn.

While climbing a fixed steel ladder from a 16-feet-deep dump pit, an employee fell 6 feet from the ladder to the steel floor of the dump pit, breaking two vertebrae and both ankles and requiring hospitalization.
An employee was cleaning windows inside a Dollar General Store when an unknown assailant entered the store, pulled out a knife, and cut the employee.

An employee was standing on top of an excavation area flagging a trench box in when the ground gave way. The employee fell inside the trench, hitting the left side of his head and back, breaking four ribs, and bruising his head.

An employee changing out a drill bit on a machine when he realized that drill bits were left inside the machine. The machine was energized at the time. While attempting to retrieve the drill bits, his left hand was struck by a moving drill.
On 9-10-15, an employee's finger was cut while inspecting a part. He was eventually hospitalized when the cut became infected.
On 9/10/15 an employee was using a table saw.  While cutting shelving, he amputated the ring finger on his left hand.

An employee was using a lashing rod to bend a piece of metal when it sprung backward, struck him in the jaw and fractured it. He fell to the ground where he also sustained lacerations to the head, eye, and neck after contacting the metal deck.
An employee was hospitalized after suffering a crushing injury when a rolling rail car ran over his toes.
An employee was sanitizing a chocolate enrober. As he attempted to unjam the chocolate pump, the pump started and amputated his left index fingertip.

The employer is contracted for all the ground and foundation work for a new grain facility.  On the day of the incident the employer was having gravel delivered to construct a road.  One of the side-dumper trucks got stuck in the ditch across from the site.  In an effort to pull the truck free the employer used one of their Caterpillar D6 dozers and two 16 foot long 5/16 inch chains.  After the first unsuccessful attempt to pull the tractor trailer free the dozer operator attempted another pull. The chain snapped flying backwards towards the dozer where the hook end crashed through the rear window and struck the employee. The employee was taken to the hospital for facial reconstruction surgery.
An employee was taking a forklift to a charging station. When he stepped off the forklift, which was still moving, his foot got caught between the forklift and a rail. His left foot was fractured.
An employee tripped and fell fracturing her left hip.
An employee was driving a forklift and struck a steel beam in the warehouse resulting in multiple injuries to his right foot.
An employee was installing a metal roof and fell 35 feet resulting in a broken arm, pelvis, and femur. The employee was hospitalized.

An employee was rolling a metal piece on an Arcotech rolling machine and got his right ring finger caught between the piece of metal and the roller. The employee's right ring finger was crushed resulting in an amputation.
An employee was operating a mule (ATV) around the fish farm. The employee attempted to stop the ATV with a foot and broke the foot.
An employee was pulling on a wild grape vine that was up in a tree. The grape vine broke and he fell to the ground, breaking his tibia and fibula.
An employee was pressure washing a house and was stung by bees. Due to a bee allergy, the employee was hospitalized.

While cleaning silage off a truck's windshield during harvesting silage operations, an employee injured his ankle when his foot got caught between the bumper and the hood of the truck, resulting in surgery and hospitalization.

On 9/11/15, employees were washing the print roller at the end of a shift. An employee bumped the right elbow on the diamond plate platform of the printing press; skin was not broken. The employee went golfing the next day and the elbow was swollen. The employee was hospitalized with an infection in the right elbow.
An employee was walking on the roof behind a buggy and was putting down stone when he hit his head on the buggy handle and fell on the roof. He injured his vertebrae.

An employee was cutting wood trim on a table saw. When the employee reached for cut scraps, their left ring finger contacted the rotating saw blade.  The employee's left index fingernail was amputated.
Employee suffered a right pinky finger amputation while using a metal stud cutting tool for carpentry work.
